\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interval MDP Parallel Construction for Controller Synthesis of Large\sphinxhyphen{}Scale Stochastic Systems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT is an open\sphinxhyphen{}source C++ tool for parallelized verification and controller synthesis
of large\sphinxhyphen{}scale stochastic systems using interval Markov decision processes (IMDPs).
Built on \sphinxhref{https://github.com/AdaptiveCpp/AdaptiveCpp}{AdaptiveCpp} (SYCL) for
adaptive parallelism across CPUs and GPUs from all hardware vendors.

\section{Installation}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/installation:installation}}\label{\detokenize{getting-started/installation::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT requires the following dependencies:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3, CMake, Boost

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/AdaptiveCpp/AdaptiveCpp}{AdaptiveCpp} (with clang++ and OpenMP)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
HDF5, \sphinxhref{https://arma.sourceforge.net}{Armadillo} (with HDF5 enabled)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
GSL, NLopt, GLPK

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The easiest way to use IMPaCT is via {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/docker::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Docker}}}}. For Ubuntu 22.04, use the
automated install script.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-set}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-item}\subsubsection*{Ubuntu 22 (Recommended)}

\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-content}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run the automated installer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
chmod\PYG{+w}{ }+x\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYGZus{}ubuntu22.sh
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }./install\PYGZus{}ubuntu22.sh
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This installs all dependencies and builds IMPaCT. See the
\sphinxhref{https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wwfP2ErgLcM\&list=PL50OJg3FHS4fBxhua92ZS3e6bxEnFaetL}{installation video}
for a walkthrough.

\end{sphinxuseclass}
\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-item}\subsubsection*{Linux (Manual)}

\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-content}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install essential build tools:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYGZhy{}essential
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Python 3 and CMake:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }python3\PYG{+w}{ }cmake
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Boost:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }libboost\PYGZhy{}all\PYGZhy{}dev
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{AdaptiveCpp:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/AdaptiveCpp/AdaptiveCpp/blob/develop/doc/installing.md}{official instructions}
for the most up\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}date guide. A copy is also bundled in the repository:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
unzip\PYG{+w}{ }AdaptiveCpp\PYGZhy{}develop.zip
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }AdaptiveCpp\PYGZhy{}develop
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}y\PYG{+w}{ }libclang\PYGZhy{}16\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }clang\PYGZhy{}tools\PYGZhy{}16\PYG{+w}{ }libomp\PYGZhy{}16\PYGZhy{}dev
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }cmake\PYG{+w}{ }.
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If issues occur, add flags such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DCMAKE\_CXX\_COMPILER=/path/to/clang++\sphinxhyphen{}16}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{HDF5:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }libhdf5\PYGZhy{}serial\PYGZhy{}dev
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Armadillo:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }libopenblas\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }liblapack\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }libarpack2\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }libsuperlu\PYGZhy{}dev
tar\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}xvf\PYG{+w}{ }armadillo\PYGZhy{}12.6.4.tar.xz
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }armadillo\PYGZhy{}12.6.4
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }cmake\PYG{+w}{ }.
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable HDF5 in Armadillo: find the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{armadillo\_bits}} directory
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo find / \sphinxhyphen{}type d \sphinxhyphen{}name \textquotesingle{}armadillo\_bits\textquotesingle{}}}), edit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config.hpp}},
and uncomment the line \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ARMA\_USE\_HDF5}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{GSL:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
tar\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}xzf\PYG{+w}{ }gsl\PYGZhy{}2.7.1.tar.gz
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }gsl\PYGZhy{}2.7.1
./configure\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }sudo\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NLopt:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
tar\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}xzf\PYG{+w}{ }nlopt\PYGZhy{}2.7.1.tar.gz
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }nlopt\PYGZhy{}2.7.1\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }mkdir\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }build
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }..\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }sudo\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{GLPK:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }glpk\PYGZhy{}utils\PYG{+w}{ }libglpk\PYGZhy{}dev
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{sphinxuseclass}
\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-item}\subsubsection*{macOS}

\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-content}
\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT has been tested on macOS with Intel chips. For Apple Silicon (M1/M2+),
check \sphinxhref{https://github.com/AdaptiveCpp/AdaptiveCpp/blob/develop/doc/installing.md}{AdaptiveCpp support}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Install dependencies via Homebrew:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
brew\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }python\PYG{+w}{ }cmake\PYG{+w}{ }boost\PYG{+w}{ }hdf5\PYG{+w}{ }gsl\PYG{+w}{ }nlopt\PYG{+w}{ }glpk
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Armadillo:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
brew\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }armadillo
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable HDF5 in Armadillo: find \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{armadillo\_bits}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sudo find / \sphinxhyphen{}type d \sphinxhyphen{}name \textquotesingle{}armadillo\_bits\textquotesingle{}}}), edit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config.hpp}},
and uncomment \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ARMA\_USE\_HDF5}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{AdaptiveCpp:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
unzip\PYG{+w}{ }AdaptiveCpp\PYGZhy{}develop.zip
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }AdaptiveCpp\PYGZhy{}develop
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }cmake\PYG{+w}{ }.\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DCMAKE\PYGZus{}INSTALL\PYGZus{}PREFIX\PYG{o}{=}/usr/local\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{              }\PYGZhy{}DCMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}COMPILER\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/clang++\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{              }\PYGZhy{}DOpenMP\PYGZus{}ROOT\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/libomp/include
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{sphinxuseclass}
\end{sphinxuseclass}
\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-item}\subsubsection*{Docker}

\begin{sphinxuseclass}{sd-tab-content}
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/docker::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Docker}}}} for container\sphinxhyphen{}based installation — no local dependencies needed.

\end{sphinxuseclass}
\end{sphinxuseclass}
\end{sphinxuseclass}

\subsection{Verification}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/installation:verification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After installation, verify by building and running an example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}2Drobot\PYGZhy{}R\PYGZhy{}U
make
./robot2D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You should see output showing the abstraction and synthesis progress.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Quick Start}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/quickstart:quick-start}}\label{\detokenize{getting-started/quickstart::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide walks through a complete example: synthesizing a controller for a 2D robot
to reach a target region. This corresponds to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ex\_2Drobot\sphinxhyphen{}R\sphinxhyphen{}U}} example.


\subsection{Prerequisites}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/quickstart:prerequisites}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ensure IMPaCT is installed (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/installation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Installation}}}}) or use {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/docker::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Docker}}}}.


\subsection{Configuration File}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/quickstart:configuration-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each IMPaCT case study is defined in a C++ configuration file. Create a file
(e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{robot2D.cpp}}) with the following structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. Include headers and set dimensions:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}../../src/IMDP.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}armadillo\PYGZgt{}}

\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{std}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{arma}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// state dimensions}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// input dimensions}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// disturbance dimensions (0 = none)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. Define the spaces:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each space is a hyper\sphinxhyphen{}rectangle defined by lower bounds, upper bounds, and discretization step sizes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// State space: [\PYGZhy{}10, 10] x [\PYGZhy{}10, 10] with step size 1}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}10}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}10}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Input space}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. Define noise and target region:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// Standard deviation of Gaussian noise per dimension}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{sqrt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.3333}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sqrt}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.3333}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Target region: square from (5,5) to (8,8)}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{4. Define dynamics:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{xx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{cos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{sin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{5. Main function — create, abstract, and synthesize:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{main}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// Create IMDP object}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// Set up spaces}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// Set dynamics and noise}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NORMAL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStdDev}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// Compute abstraction}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{targetTransitionVectorBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsection{Build and Run}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/quickstart:build-and-run}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}2Drobot\PYGZhy{}R\PYGZhy{}U
make
./robot2D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The tool will output progress for the abstraction and synthesis steps. Results are
saved as HDF5 files in the same directory.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Suppress debug output with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export ACPP\_DEBUG\_LEVEL=0}} before running.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Output Files}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/quickstart:output-files}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT saves results in HDF5 format (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.h5}} files):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss.h5}} — state space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{is.h5}} — input space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts.h5}} — target space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minTM.h5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{maxTM.h5}} — transition matrix bounds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{controller.h5}} — synthesized controller

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These can be loaded in MATLAB, Python, or R for visualization.
See the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{misc/}} folder for plotting utilities.

\section{Docker}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/docker:docker}}\label{\detokenize{getting-started/docker::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The easiest way to use IMPaCT is via Docker — no local dependency installation required.


\subsection{Building the Image}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/docker:building-the-image}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }impact\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first build may take a while as it compiles all dependencies.


\subsection{Running the Container}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/docker:running-the-container}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}it\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }impact\PYG{+w}{ }impact
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This opens a shell inside the container. Run examples with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }/app/examples/ex\PYGZus{}2Drobot\PYGZhy{}R\PYGZhy{}U
make
./robot2D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Mounting a Volume}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/docker:mounting-a-volume}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To use your own examples or persist results, mount a local directory:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}it\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }impact\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/my\PYGZhy{}examples:/app/examples\PYG{+w}{ }impact
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Files are shared between the container and host, so results appear in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}/my\sphinxhyphen{}examples}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Files created inside the container (not in a mounted volume) are lost when the
container stops.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Copying Results}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/docker:copying-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively, copy files out of a running container:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }cp\PYG{+w}{ }impact:/app/examples/ex\PYGZus{}2Drobot\PYGZhy{}R\PYGZhy{}U/controller.h5\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{GPU Setup}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/gpu:gpu-setup}}\label{\detokenize{getting-started/gpu::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT supports GPU\sphinxhyphen{}accelerated synthesis via AdaptiveCpp’s SYCL implementation.
GPU acceleration applies to the \sphinxstylestrong{sorted synthesis algorithms} — abstraction is
computed on the CPU and loaded from file.


\subsection{Prerequisites}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/gpu:prerequisites}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install the base IMPaCT dependencies first (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/installation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Installation}}}}), then add
GPU\sphinxhyphen{}specific libraries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify your GPU:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
lspci\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }grep\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}i\PYG{+w}{ }vga
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{LLVM}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/gpu:llvm}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
wget\PYG{+w}{ }https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh
chmod\PYG{+w}{ }+x\PYG{+w}{ }llvm.sh
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }./llvm.sh\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{16}
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}y\PYG{+w}{ }libclang\PYGZhy{}16\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }clang\PYGZhy{}tools\PYGZhy{}16\PYG{+w}{ }libomp\PYGZhy{}16\PYGZhy{}dev\PYG{+w}{ }llvm\PYGZhy{}16\PYGZhy{}dev
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{CUDA (NVIDIA)}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/gpu:cuda-nvidia}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }nvidia\PYGZhy{}cuda\PYGZhy{}toolkit
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Verify with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nvcc \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}version}}.


\subsection{Rebuild AdaptiveCpp with GPU Support}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/gpu:rebuild-adaptivecpp-with-gpu-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After installing GPU libraries, rebuild AdaptiveCpp with the appropriate flags:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }AdaptiveCpp\PYGZhy{}develop
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }cmake\PYG{+w}{ }.\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DCUDAToolkit\PYGZus{}LIBRARY\PYGZus{}ROOT\PYG{o}{=}/usr/lib/cuda
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }make\PYG{+w}{ }install
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/AdaptiveCpp/AdaptiveCpp/blob/develop/doc/installing.md}{AdaptiveCpp documentation}
for other GPU backends (Intel, AMD).


\subsection{Makefile Changes}
\label{\detokenize{getting-started/gpu:makefile-changes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To use GPU synthesis, update your example’s Makefile:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the target from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}acpp\sphinxhyphen{}targets="omp"}} to your GPU target
(e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cuda:sm\_70}} for NVIDIA V100).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replace \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMDP.cpp}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GPU\_synthesis.cpp}} in the source files.

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{CC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }acpp
\PYG{n+nv}{CFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}acpp\PYGZhy{}targets\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}cuda:sm\PYGZus{}70\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O3\PYG{+w}{ }...
\PYG{n+nv}{SRCS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }example.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }../../src/GPU\PYGZus{}synthesis.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }../../src/MDP.cpp
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
GPU synthesis requires pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed abstraction matrices loaded from file.
Compute the abstraction on CPU first, save to HDF5, then load for GPU synthesis.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{user-guide/io::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Loading and Saving}}}} for details.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Configuration}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:configuration}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each IMPaCT case study is defined in a C++ configuration file (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{robot2D.cpp}}).
This page explains every configurable component.


\subsection{IMDP Object}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:imdp-object}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create an IMDP object specifying the dimensions of each space:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{imdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dim\_x}} — state space dimensions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dim\_u}} — input space dimensions (set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for IMC verification)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dim\_w}} — disturbance space dimensions (set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} if none)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dim\_u = 0}}, IMPaCT automatically treats the problem as IMC verification
and returns satisfaction probabilities instead of a controller.


\subsection{State, Input, and Disturbance Spaces}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:state-input-and-disturbance-spaces}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each space is a hyper\sphinxhyphen{}rectangle defined by three vectors of length equal to the
number of dimensions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setDisturbSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lb}} — lower bound of each dimension

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ub}} — upper bound of each dimension

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eta}} — discretization step size of each dimension

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If input or disturbance spaces are not present, simply omit the call.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}10}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{\PYGZhy{}10}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Target and Avoid Regions}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:target-and-avoid-regions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, all states are considered safe. For reachability or reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid
specifications, define target and/or avoid regions using boolean functions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{condition}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remove}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setAvoidSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{condition}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remove}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setTargetAvoidSpace}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{avoid\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remove}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{remove = true}} to move matching states out of the state space (typical usage).
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{remove = false}} to keep them in the state space (useful for counting states).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// Target: square region from (5,5) to (8,8)}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{8.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:dynamics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Define system dynamics as a lambda function. The number of parameters must match
the IMDP object dimensions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// 3 parameters: state, input, disturbance}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// 2 parameters: state, input (no disturbance)}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// 1 parameter: state only (autonomous system)}
\PYG{k+kt}{void}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{function}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{d}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT detects the number of parameters automatically.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{xx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{cos}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{sin}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Noise Distributions}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:noise-distributions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT supports three noise configurations:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Normal distribution with diagonal covariance (default):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NORMAL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStdDev}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// vec of standard deviations}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses the closed\sphinxhyphen{}form CDF product, which is the fastest option.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multivariate normal with full covariance:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NORMAL}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setInvCovDet}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{inv\PYGZus{}cov}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{det}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// inverse covariance + determinant}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses Monte Carlo integration with the specified number of samples.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Custom distribution:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Edit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/custom.cpp}} to define your PDF, then:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CUSTOM}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The custom PDF receives a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{customParams}} struct with access to the current state,
dynamics, input, disturbance, integration bounds, and discretization parameter.


\subsection{Optimization Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:optimization-algorithm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The nonlinear optimization algorithm for abstraction can be changed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setAlgorithm}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nlopt}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{LN\PYGZus{}SBPLX}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// default}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the \sphinxhref{https://nlopt.readthedocs.io/en/latest/NLopt\_Algorithms/}{NLopt documentation}
for other algorithms (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LN\_COBYLA}}).


\subsection{Stopping Condition}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/configuration:stopping-condition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the convergence threshold for infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon synthesis:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStoppingCondition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.00001}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// default}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Verification and Synthesis}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:verification-and-synthesis}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After configuring the system and computing the abstraction, IMPaCT performs
formal verification or controller synthesis using interval iteration algorithms.


\subsection{Abstraction}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:abstraction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The abstraction computes transition probability bounds for every state\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}state pair.
These are always required:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// Transition matrices (state\PYGZhy{}to\PYGZhy{}state)}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Avoid transition vectors (state\PYGZhy{}to\PYGZhy{}outside)}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For reachability or reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid specifications, also compute target vectors:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minTargetTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxTargetTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Low\sphinxhyphen{}Cost Abstraction}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:low-cost-abstraction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For sparse systems, a computational trick can speed up the abstraction: if the
maximal transition probability is zero, the minimal must also be zero. Use these
functions to exploit this:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{transitionMatrixBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{// replaces separate min/max calls}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{targetTransitionVectorBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{// replaces separate min/max calls}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The sparser the system, the greater the speedup.


\subsection{Controller Synthesis}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:controller-synthesis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT provides synthesis for two specification types across two time horizons.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All functions take a boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMDP\_lower}} parameter:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} — \sphinxstylestrong{pessimistic} strategy (worst\sphinxhyphen{}case noise, lower bound probabilities)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} — \sphinxstylestrong{optimistic} strategy (best\sphinxhyphen{}case noise, upper bound probabilities)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Infinite\sphinxhyphen{}Horizon}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:infinite-horizon}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses the \sphinxstylestrong{interval iteration} algorithm with convergence guarantees:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infiniteHorizonReachController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// reachability / reach\PYGZhy{}avoid}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infiniteHorizonSafeController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{// safety}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid is detected automatically when an avoid region has been defined.


\subsubsection{Finite\sphinxhyphen{}Horizon}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:finite-horizon}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses \sphinxstylestrong{value iteration} for a specified number of time steps:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{finiteHorizonReachController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// 10 time steps}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{finiteHorizonSafeController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Sorted Synthesis (GPU\sphinxhyphen{}Compatible)}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:sorted-synthesis-gpu-compatible}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorted variants remove the dependency on the GLPK library and enable GPU execution:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infiniteHorizonReachControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infiniteHorizonSafeControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{finiteHorizonReachControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{finiteHorizonSafeControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These functions are implemented in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/GPU\_synthesis.cpp}}. To use them on a GPU,
update the Makefile (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/gpu::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{GPU Setup}}}}).

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
GPU synthesis requires pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed abstraction matrices loaded from HDF5 files.
Compute the abstraction on CPU first, then load for GPU synthesis.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{user-guide/io::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Loading and Saving}}}} for save/load details.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{IMC Verification}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/synthesis:imc-verification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the input dimension is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} (no control inputs), IMPaCT automatically
performs \sphinxstylestrong{verification} instead of synthesis. The same functions are used —
the output is a lookup table of satisfaction probabilities rather than a controller.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{imdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// 7D system, no inputs, no disturbance}
\PYG{c+c1}{// ... set state space, dynamics, noise ...}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infiniteHorizonSafeController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{// returns probabilities}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Loading and Saving}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/io:loading-and-saving}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/io::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT uses \sphinxhref{https://www.hdfgroup.org/solutions/hdf5/}{HDF5} for all data
persistence. This enables interoperability with MATLAB, Python (h5py), R (rhdf5),
and other tools. The HDF5 field name is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dataset}} by default.


\subsection{Saving Data}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/io:saving-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save any component after it has been computed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// Spaces}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} ss.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} is.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveDisturbSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} ws.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{       }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} ts.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveAvoidSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} as.h5}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Transition matrices and vectors}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveMinTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} minTM.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveMaxTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} maxTM.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveMinTargetTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} minTV.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveMaxTargetTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} maxTV.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveMinAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} minAV.h5}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveMaxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{// \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} maxAV.h5}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Controller}

\subsection{Loading Data}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/io:loading-data}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed data from HDF5 files:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{// Spaces}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ss.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{is.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadDisturbSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ws.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ts.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadAvoidSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{as.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Transition matrices and vectors}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMinTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{minTM.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMaxTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maxTM.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMinTargetTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{minTV.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMaxTargetTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maxTV.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMinAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{minAV.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMaxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maxAV.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Controller}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{controller.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is useful for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{GPU synthesis}: compute abstraction on CPU, load on GPU for synthesis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data\sphinxhyphen{}driven methods}: load transition matrices computed externally

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Resuming computation}: save intermediate results and continue later

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{misc/}} folder contains MATLAB, Python, and R utilities for reading
HDF5 files and plotting results.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Debugging Tips}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/io:debugging-tips}}
\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If synthesis diverges to values greater than 1, your loaded matrices may need
to be \sphinxstylestrong{transposed}. Use tools like MATLAB’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{h5disp}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{h5read}} to
verify dimensions before loading.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the controller shows both upper and lower bounds as zero, this indicates an
\sphinxstylestrong{infeasible solution} — typically because a minimal value exceeds a maximal
value somewhere. Verify that max \textgreater{}= min for all entries.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Makefiles}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/makefiles:makefiles}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/makefiles::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each IMPaCT example uses a Makefile to compile the configuration file with all
dependencies. Understanding the Makefile structure helps when creating new examples
or troubleshooting build issues.


\subsection{Structure}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/makefiles:structure}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A typical Makefile compiles a command equivalent to:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
acpp\PYG{+w}{ }robot2D.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }../../src/IMDP.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }../../src/MDP.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}acpp\PYGZhy{}targets\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}omp\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}lnlopt\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}I/usr/include/hdf5/serial\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}L/usr/lib/x86\PYGZus{}64\PYGZhy{}linux\PYGZhy{}gnu/hdf5/serial\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}lhdf5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lglpk\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lgsl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lgslcblas\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}DH5\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}110\PYGZus{}API\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}larmadillo\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}o\PYG{+w}{ }robot2D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Key Components}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/makefiles:key-components}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compiler}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{acpp}} (AdaptiveCpp). Also works with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{syclcc}} in some cases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Targets}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}acpp\sphinxhyphen{}targets="omp"}} selects OpenMP as the parallelism backend.
For GPU, replace with your target (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cuda:sm\_70}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Source files}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Your configuration file (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{robot2D.cpp}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{../../src/IMDP.cpp}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{../../src/MDP.cpp}} — core library files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For GPU: replace \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMDP.cpp}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GPU\_synthesis.cpp}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Linker flags} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}l}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lnlopt}} — NLopt optimization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lm}} — math library

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lhdf5}} — HDF5 data storage

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lglpk}} — GLPK linear programming (not needed for sorted synthesis)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lgsl \sphinxhyphen{}lgslcblas}} — GNU Scientific Library

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}larmadillo}} — Armadillo linear algebra

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Include/Library paths} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}I}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}L}}):

\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicit paths to HDF5 headers and libraries. Adjust these if HDF5 is installed
in a different location on your system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Preprocessor}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}DH5\_USE\_110\_API}} selects the HDF5 1.10 API.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Optimization}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}O3}} enables maximum compiler optimization.


\subsection{Creating a New Example}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/makefiles:creating-a-new-example}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a new directory under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copy a Makefile from an existing example.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Update the source file name in the Makefile.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ensure the relative paths to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{../../src/}} are correct.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make}} and then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./your\_executable}}.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/makefiles:troubleshooting}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Library not found}: add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}I}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}L}} flags pointing to the correct paths.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compiler issues}: try \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{syclcc}} instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{acpp}}, or vice versa.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Debug output}: set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export ACPP\_DEBUG\_LEVEL=0}} to suppress AdaptiveCpp warnings.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See the \sphinxhref{https://opensource.com/article/18/8/what-how-makefile}{Makefile guide}
for general Makefile help.

\end{itemize}

\section{Feature Manual (v2.0)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/index:feature-manual-v2-0}}\label{\detokenize{manual/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual documents every verification and synthesis feature of IMPaCT v2.0 beyond
the abstraction front end: what each feature computes (with precise robust semantics),
the literature algorithm it implements, a validated CLI example, and how it compares to
the peer tools \sphinxstylestrong{PRISM 4.8.1}, \sphinxstylestrong{Storm 1.13.0}, and \sphinxstylestrong{IntervalMDP.jl 0.6}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Everything here runs through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tools/imdp\_solve}}, the dependency\sphinxhyphen{}free CLI over the
neutral \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} exchange format (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/formats::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{File Formats and Converters}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/cli::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{CLI Reference: imdp\_solve}}}}). Every numeric value
quoted in this manual was produced by a live run against the models in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/models/}} and cross\sphinxhyphen{}checked against the reference values in the
matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*.ref.json}} files; cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool methodology is in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}} at the repository root.


\subsection{Conventions}
\label{\detokenize{manual/index:conventions}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pess} (pessimistic / robust): the controller maximises the objective while nature
resolves every transition\sphinxhyphen{}probability interval \sphinxstyleemphasis{adversarially} — the value a
controller can \sphinxstyleemphasis{guarantee} for all distributions within the intervals.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{opt} (optimistic): nature resolves the intervals \sphinxstyleemphasis{cooperatively} — the best case.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Solvers return a \sphinxstylestrong{sound bracket} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}lower, upper{]}}} with gap \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}= 2*eps}} (default
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eps = 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6}}); finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon dynamic programming is exact.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The shared inner solve for all robust Bellman backups is \sphinxstylestrong{O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization}
(Givan, Leach, Dean, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bounded\sphinxhyphen{}parameter MDPs}, AIJ 2000; Lahijanian, Andersson,
Belta, IEEE TAC 2015), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/omaximization.h}}.

\end{itemize}

\section{Probabilistic Specifications}
\label{\detokenize{manual/specifications:probabilistic-specifications}}\label{\detokenize{manual/specifications::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reachability, safety, reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid, step\sphinxhyphen{}bounded reachability, and the PCTL path
operators on interval MDPs (IMDPs).


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/specifications:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For an IMDP, the controller maximises the probability of the path property while
\sphinxstyleemphasis{nature} picks, at every step, a transition distribution within the per\sphinxhyphen{}successor
probability intervals:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pessimistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound pess}}, default): nature is adversarial. The result is the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{robust} value — a guarantee that holds for every distribution in the intervals.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{optimistic} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound opt}}): nature is cooperative — the best\sphinxhyphen{}case value.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All unbounded properties return a sound sandwich \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower \textless{}= V*(s) \textless{}= upper}} with gap
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}= 2*eps}}; finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}horizon k}}) properties are computed by exact dynamic
programming (no gap). Properties:

\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/specifications:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The inner robust Bellman solve \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opt\_\{p in {[}lo,hi{]}\} Σ p(s\textquotesingle{})V(s\textquotesingle{})}} is \sphinxstylestrong{O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization}
(closed\sphinxhyphen{}form sort\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}assign), from Givan, Leach, Dean, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bounded\sphinxhyphen{}parameter Markov
decision processes}, Artificial Intelligence, 2000, and Lahijanian, Andersson, Belta,
IEEE Trans. Automatic Control, 2015 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/omaximization.h}}, verified against
brute\sphinxhyphen{}force vertex enumeration).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The outer fixpoint (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.h}}) is solved by one of two methods (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/engines::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Solver Engines}}}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Optimistic value iteration} (default) — Hartmanns \& Kaminski, CAV 2020: VI from
below plus a verified inductive (pre\sphinxhyphen{}fixpoint) upper bound.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interval iteration with end\sphinxhyphen{}component collapse} — Baier et al., CAV 2017;
Haddad \& Monmege, TCS 2018.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
PCTL operators (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{next}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{until}}, bounded until; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/pctl.h}}) follow Hansson \& Jonsson
(Formal Aspects of Computing, 1994); the robust interval\sphinxhyphen{}MDP reading follows Puggelli,
Li, Sangiovanni\sphinxhyphen{}Vincentelli, Seshia, CAV 2013, and Baier \& Katoen, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Principles of Model
Checking}, Ch. 10.

\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/specifications:peer-tools-and-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Robust reachability/safety is the one query all four tools support. On the shared
models (identical \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} exported to each tool’s native format) \sphinxstylestrong{IMPaCT ==
IntervalMDP.jl == PRISM == Storm}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chain\_point}} 0.25, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{safety\_point}} 0.72,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choice\_interval}} 0.4/0.5, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fork\_interval}} 0.4/0.6, and the 207\sphinxhyphen{}state
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multiObj\_robotIMDP}} 0.894663 (agreement \textasciitilde{}1e\sphinxhyphen{}6); see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} \S{}1 and the
ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP 2025 sweep (\S{}2), where all four agree on every robust value. Step\sphinxhyphen{}bounded
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P{[}F\textless{}=k{]}}} was validated against Storm \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmax=?{[}F\textless{}=k "goal"{]}}} for k = 1, 2, 3
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounded\_demo.ref.json}}). PRISM peers require the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmaxmin}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmaxmax}} query form and
reject interval edges with a 0 lower bound (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/formats::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{File Formats and Converters}}}}).


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/specifications:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pessimistic interval iteration alone does not converge on \sphinxstyleemphasis{nature\sphinxhyphen{}confinable} end
components (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0003, resolved by the OVI default; see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/engines::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Solver Engines}}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
OVI can be slow on large strongly\sphinxhyphen{}recurrent IMDPs, mainly in the optimistic sense
(ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0010, now largely mitigated by topological Gauss\textendash{}Seidel — BA at 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 went from \textgreater{}180 s to 7.8 s); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}method mec}} remains an alternative.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The optimistic sense is convention\sphinxhyphen{}dependent across tools for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}} “leak” edges
(ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0018, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} \S{}4); the robust value is unambiguous and is the
headline number.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_solve}} exposes controller\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxstyleemphasis{maximising} queries (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmax}}); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmin}} flavours are
future work (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/pctl.h}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Expected Rewards}
\label{\detokenize{manual/rewards:expected-rewards}}\label{\detokenize{manual/rewards::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Robust expected total reward on interval MDPs: \sphinxstylestrong{reachability reward} (accumulate
until a target is reached) and \sphinxstylestrong{discounted reward}.


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/rewards:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
State rewards are given by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward \textless{}s\textgreater{} \textless{}v\textgreater{}}} lines in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} file (missing states
default to 0). The controller maximises the expected accumulated reward; nature
resolves the transition intervals adversarially (pess) or cooperatively (opt) on the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{continuation value} via O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reachability reward} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward LABEL}}, discount γ = 1): expected total state reward
accumulated until the target set is first reached. The target is absorbing and
reward stops there. Bellman recursion (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.h}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
V(s) = reward[s] + max\PYGZus{}a  opt\PYGZus{}\PYGZob{}p in [lo,hi]\PYGZcb{} Σ\PYGZus{}s\PYGZsq{} p(s\PYGZsq{}) V(s\PYGZsq{}),    V(target) = 0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{+\(\infty\) semantics:} if the target is not reached almost surely and rewards are
positive, the value diverges; IMPaCT reports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HUGE\_VAL}} (prints \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inf}}), matching
PRISM/Storm’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Infinity}} convention for stochastic\sphinxhyphen{}shortest\sphinxhyphen{}path divergence.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Discounted reward} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward LABEL \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}discount g}}, γ ∈ (0,1)):
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{V(s) = reward{[}s{]} + γ · max\_a opt\_p Σ p V}}. This is a contraction, so it always
converges and needs no target (the label argument is still required syntactically).
This is the objective IntervalMDP.jl natively supports.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected time / expected steps to reach} is the special case of reachability reward
with unit state rewards (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward s 1}} for every non\sphinxhyphen{}target state), as noted in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}}.


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/rewards:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Robust dynamic programming over the interval ambiguity set, with the inner
minimisation/maximisation solved in closed form by O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iyengar, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Robust Dynamic Programming}, Mathematics of Operations Research, 2005.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nilim \& El Ghaoui, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Robust control of MDPs with uncertain transition matrices},
Operations Research, 2005.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Givan, Leach, Dean, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bounded\sphinxhyphen{}parameter MDPs}, AIJ 2000 (the interval inner solve).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Puterman, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Markov Decision Processes}, 1994 (SSP finiteness for the γ = 1 case).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convergence certification: interval iteration / OVI (Baier et al. CAV 2017;
Hartmanns \& Kaminski CAV 2020), as for reachability.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implementation: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solve::expReachReward}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solve::expDiscountedReward}} and the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{maxReachReward\{Pessimistic,Optimistic\}}} wrappers in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.\{h,cpp\}}}.


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/rewards:cli-examples-validated}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward\_chain}} model has r(s0)=1, r(s1)=2; from s1 nature chooses to move to the
target with probability in {[}0.5, 1.0{]} or stay with {[}0.0, 0.5{]}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Reachability reward: pess (nature leaves s1 asap) V0 = 3; opt (nature stays) V0 = 5}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/reward\PYGZus{}chain.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reward\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reward  bound=pess  state=0  lower=3            upper=3            iters=3}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reward  bound=opt   state=0  lower=4.999999046  upper=4.999999046  iters=23}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Discounted reward, gamma = 0.9: pess 2.8, opt 2/(1\PYGZhy{}0.45)*0.9+1 = 4.2727...}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/reward\PYGZus{}chain.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reward\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}discount\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.9\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reward  bound=pess  state=0  lower=2.8          upper=2.8          iters=3}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reward  bound=opt   state=0  lower=4.272726893  upper=4.272726893  iters=21}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both match the analytic hand values in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward\_chain.ref.json}} (3 / 5 and
2.8 / 4.272727).


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/rewards:peer-tools-and-validation}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM 4.8.1}: interval reachability reward via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmaxmin}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmaxmax}} — matches
IMPaCT (3.000000002 / 4.999996 on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward\_chain}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IntervalMDP.jl 0.6}: discounted reward only (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{InfiniteTimeReward}} requires
discount \textless{} 1) — matches IMPaCT to 9+ digits (2.8 / 4.272726893).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Storm 1.13.0}: its interval reward \sphinxstylestrong{ignores} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}resolution}} and
returns only the nature\sphinxhyphen{}max value (4.999996 = the optimistic value); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmin}} on
intervals is unsupported. Documented in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward\_chain.ref.json}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} \S{}1b.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT is the only tool providing \sphinxstyleemphasis{both} robust senses for \sphinxstyleemphasis{both} reward objectives on
interval MDPs.


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/rewards:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rewards are \sphinxstylestrong{state\sphinxhyphen{}based} only (no action or transition rewards in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}}
format).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reward objectives are not yet available in the multi\sphinxhyphen{}objective engine
({\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/multiobjective::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Objective Verification}}}}) — a documented refinement in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ROADMAP\_UPGRADES.md}} \S{}3.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Divergent (+\(\infty\)) reachability\sphinxhyphen{}reward cases are reported but not distinguished from
very large finite values until convergence is abandoned; use the discounted variant
when the target is not reached almost surely.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Long\sphinxhyphen{}Run Average and Steady\sphinxhyphen{}State}
\label{\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate:long-run-average-and-steady-state}}\label{\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Robust long\sphinxhyphen{}run average (mean\sphinxhyphen{}payoff) reward and steady\sphinxhyphen{}state probabilities on
interval MDPs — the interval/robust versions are unique to IMPaCT.


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate:what-is-computed}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lra}}} — the robust long\sphinxhyphen{}run average reward
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lim inf (1/T) Σ\_\{t\textless{}T\} r(s\_t)}}, controller maximising, nature resolving the
intervals adversarially (pess) or cooperatively (opt) at every step.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss LABEL}}} — the steady\sphinxhyphen{}state (long\sphinxhyphen{}run fraction of time) probability of the
states labelled \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LABEL}}. IMPaCT computes it as the \sphinxstylestrong{long\sphinxhyphen{}run average of the
indicator reward} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1\_LABEL}}, the classical identity (Baier \& Katoen, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Principles of
Model Checking}, Ch. 10; Puterman 1994) — this is PRISM’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}} operator, generalised
to robust interval MDPs.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two\sphinxhyphen{}phase value iteration (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solve::longRunAverage}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.\{h,cpp\}}}):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{MEC gain}: the robust average reward (gain) of each maximal end component is
computed by \sphinxstyleemphasis{relative value iteration} with Puterman’s aperiodicity transform
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L\_τ h = (1\sphinxhyphen{}τ)h + τ(r + opt\_a opt\_p Σ p·h)}}, restricted to each MEC’s staying
actions (support ⊆ MEC — exactly why nature cannot escape it). The interval
ambiguity set is resolved by O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cash\sphinxhyphen{}out}: a max\sphinxhyphen{}reachability VI funnels every state to the best
robustly\sphinxhyphen{}reachable MEC gain.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Literature (verified in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ROADMAP\_UPGRADES.md}} \S{}2):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ashok, Chatterjee, Daca, Křetínský, Meggendorfer, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Value Iteration for Long\sphinxhyphen{}Run
Average Reward in MDPs}, CAV 2017 (arXiv:1705.02326) — the two\sphinxhyphen{}phase VI.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Chatterjee, Goharshady, Karrabi, Novotný, Žikelić, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Solving Long\sphinxhyphen{}run Average Reward
Robust MDPs via Stochastic Games}, IJCAI 2024 (arXiv:2312.13912) — the
robust/interval setting (that work uses policy iteration/games; IMPaCT takes the VI
route).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Puterman, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Markov Decision Processes}, 1994, Ch. 8 (average\sphinxhyphen{}reward optimality,
relative VI, aperiodicity transform); Iyengar 2005 (robust inner solve).

\end{itemize}


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate:cli-examples-validated}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Point 2\PYGZhy{}cycle, r(0)=1, r(1)=3: mean payoff (1+3)/2 = 2 (== Storm R\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}r\PYGZdq{}\PYGZcb{}max=?[LRA])}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/lra\PYGZus{}cycle.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }lra\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=lra  bound=pess  state=0  lower=2  upper=2  iters=0}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Interval MEC, r(0)=4, r(1)=0, stay [0.5,1]/switch [0,0.5]: nature traps the play in}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} state 1 (robust gain 0) or keeps it in state 0 (optimistic gain 4). IMPaCT\PYGZhy{}only.}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/lra\PYGZus{}interval.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }lra\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=lra  bound=pess  state=0  lower=2.265286626e\PYGZhy{}06  upper=2.265286626e\PYGZhy{}06  iters=0}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=lra  bound=opt   state=0  lower=4                upper=4                iters=0}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Steady\PYGZhy{}state: DTMC with stationary distribution (4/7, 3/7); S(g=\PYGZob{}1\PYGZcb{}) = 3/7}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/ss\PYGZus{}dtmc.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }ss\PYG{+w}{ }g
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=ss  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0.4285698197  upper=0.4285698197  iters=0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lra}} property takes no target label — pass \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}} as the LABEL placeholder. Values
match the analytic references 2, 0 / 4, and 3/7 = 0.4285714 within the VI tolerance
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lra\_cycle.ref.json}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lra\_interval.ref.json}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss\_dtmc.ref.json}}).


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate:peer-tools-and-validation}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Storm} computes point\sphinxhyphen{}model LRA (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{R\{"r"\}max=? {[}LRA{]}}} = 2 on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lra\_cycle}}, matching
IMPaCT) and steady\sphinxhyphen{}state (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S=? {[}g{]}}} = 0.4285714286 on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss\_dtmc}}, matching IMPaCT),
but reports \sphinxstyleemphasis{“LRA with intervals not implemented”} for interval models.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM}’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}} operator is DTMC/CTMC\sphinxhyphen{}only (no MDP steady\sphinxhyphen{}state reward, no interval
LRA).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IntervalMDP.jl} has no LRA / steady\sphinxhyphen{}state objective.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Robust interval LRA and robust steady\sphinxhyphen{}state were therefore validated against the
analytic hand values (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lra\_interval}} 0 / 4) — \sphinxstylestrong{an IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}only capability}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} \S{}1b).


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convergence of the gain phase is controlled by the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}eps}}; the robust
pessimistic value on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lra\_interval}} converges to \textasciitilde{}2e\sphinxhyphen{}6 rather than exactly 0
(residual of the relative VI) — tighten \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}eps}} for sharper values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The steady\sphinxhyphen{}state of a \sphinxstyleemphasis{multichain} interval MDP is the reachability\sphinxhyphen{}weighted best
MEC gain (phase 2), i.e. the controller\sphinxhyphen{}optimal long\sphinxhyphen{}run frequency; per\sphinxhyphen{}initial
distribution steady\sphinxhyphen{}state vectors are not exposed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
An exact policy\sphinxhyphen{}iteration LRA (as in Chatterjee et al., IJCAI 2024) is a documented
refinement (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ROADMAP\_UPGRADES.md}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope
