\sphinxAtStartPar
Pessimistic = the controller wins against \sphinxstyleemphasis{every} nature resolution; optimistic =
nature cooperates.


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/omega-ltl:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Büchi} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/omega.h}}) reduces to reachability of accepting end components — the
classical reduction (de Alfaro, PhD thesis, 1997; Baier \& Katoen, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Principles of Model
Checking}, Ch. 10). The two senses differ structurally:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Optimistic}: support\sphinxhyphen{}graph accepting MECs (exact for that sense and point MDPs).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pessimistic (robust)}: support MECs are \sphinxstylestrong{unsound} — inside a support EC nature can
route around the accepting state using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lo=0}} edges (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0009). IMPaCT computes the
robust almost\sphinxhyphen{}sure\sphinxhyphen{}Büchi winning region by a nested fixpoint of robust EC closure and
robust almost\sphinxhyphen{}sure reachability — the qualitative 2.5\sphinxhyphen{}player Büchi computation
(Chatterjee\sphinxhyphen{}Henzinger graph games; the IMDP reading follows Dutreix\sphinxhyphen{}Coogan permanent
components and Asadi et al. force attractors) — then robust reachability of it.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Persistence} F G p is robust reachability of the largest controllably\sphinxhyphen{}invariant
sub\sphinxhyphen{}region of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}}; \sphinxstylestrong{patrol} is degeneralized to Büchi by a round\sphinxhyphen{}robin counter
product.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Arbitrary LTL} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltlx}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/ltl\_spot.h}}): a \sphinxstylestrong{two\sphinxhyphen{}stage} pipeline covering \sphinxstyleemphasis{all of
LTL} (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0016, resolved 2026\sphinxhyphen{}07\sphinxhyphen{}02):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
translate the formula with Spot’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl2tgba \sphinxhyphen{}D}} (Duret\sphinxhyphen{}Lutz et al., \sphinxstyleemphasis{Spot 2.0});

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
if the result is a \sphinxstylestrong{deterministic (generalized) Büchi} automaton: synchronous
product with the IMDP (a deterministic automaton is always good\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}MDPs — Hahn,
Perez, Schewe, Somenzi, Trivedi, Wojtczak, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Good\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}MDPs Automata}, TACAS 2020 —
so the product value is the LTL value), solved robustly with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega::maxGenBuchi\{Pessimistic,Optimistic\}}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
otherwise (co\sphinxhyphen{}Büchi \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F G}}\sphinxhyphen{}type and beyond) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltlx}} \sphinxstylestrong{falls back automatically} to a
\sphinxstylestrong{limit\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic Büchi automaton} from Owl’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl2ldba}} (Křetínský,
Meggendorfer, Sickert, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Owl: A Library for ω\sphinxhyphen{}Words, Automata, and LTL}, ATVA 2018,
DOI 10.1007/978\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}030\sphinxhyphen{}01090\sphinxhyphen{}4\_34; LDBA theory: Sickert, Esparza, Jaax, Křetínský,
CAV 2016). The LDBA’s ε\sphinxhyphen{}jumps to its accepting component appear as same\sphinxhyphen{}letter
nondeterminism, which the product resolves by the \sphinxstylestrong{controller} — each matching
automaton edge multiplies the product action space (sound because such LDBAs are
good\sphinxhyphen{}for\sphinxhyphen{}MDPs, Hahn et al. TACAS 2020); transition\sphinxhyphen{}based Büchi marks become
state\sphinxhyphen{}based accepting \sphinxstyleemphasis{entry copies}, and the same robust Büchi engine applies
unchanged.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Owl fallback is enabled by pointing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMPACT\_LTL2LDBA}} at Owl’s native binary
(no JRE needed for the Linux amd64 release):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{IMPACT\PYGZus{}LTL2LDBA}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}/opt/owl/owl\PYGZhy{}linux\PYGZhy{}musl\PYGZhy{}amd64\PYGZhy{}21.0/bin/owl ltl2ldba\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Without it, nondeterministic\sphinxhyphen{}automaton formulas are rejected soundly with an error
suggesting the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl}} fragment (which covers persistence) as the dependency\sphinxhyphen{}free
alternative.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the environment variable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMPACT\_LTL2TGBA}} to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl2tgba}} command if it is not
on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PATH}} (it may embed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LD\_LIBRARY\_PATH=... .../ltl2tgba}}).


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/omega-ltl:cli-examples-validated}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Robust vs optimistic Büchi where nature can route around the accepting state}

0.5 / 1.0, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{patrol\_cycle}} 1.0; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl\_demo}} point MDP \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F a}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{G F a}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X X a}} = 0.5 and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{G (a \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} X a)}} = 1.0 (all \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*.ref.json}}).


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/omega-ltl:peer-tools-and-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No peer does robust ω\sphinxhyphen{}regular on intervals: Storm reports \sphinxstyleemphasis{“LTL with intervals not
implemented”}, PRISM \sphinxstyleemphasis{“Computation not implemented yet”}, IntervalMDP.jl supports only
DFA/co\sphinxhyphen{}safe reachability. Validation is therefore two\sphinxhyphen{}legged (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}}
\S{}1, \S{}1b): on \sphinxstylestrong{point} MDPs, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltlx}} values equal Storm \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmax=?{[}φ{]}}} for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F a}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{G F a}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X X a}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{G(a\(\rightarrow\)X a)}}; on \sphinxstylestrong{interval} models the values match the exact analytic
references above. The robust\sphinxhyphen{}Büchi core (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0009) is oracle\sphinxhyphen{}validated separately.


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/omega-ltl:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltlx}} covers \sphinxstylestrong{all of LTL}: the deterministic\sphinxhyphen{}(generalized\sphinxhyphen{})Büchi class via Spot,
and the nondeterministic class (co\sphinxhyphen{}Büchi \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F G}} etc.) via Owl’s limit\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic
automata with the controller\sphinxhyphen{}resolved jump product (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0016, resolved; validated
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F G a}} = persistence solver = Storm on the point model, and 0.3/0.7 analytically on
the interval model). LDBAs with \sphinxstyleemphasis{generalized} (multi\sphinxhyphen{}set) acceptance are not yet
handled by the fallback (Owl’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl2ldba}} emits single\sphinxhyphen{}set Büchi).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltlx}} requires external translators (Spot’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl2tgba}}; Owl’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl2ldba}} for the
fallback); the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ltl}} fragment has no external dependency.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
On unbounded\sphinxhyphen{}noise abstractions the infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon ω\sphinxhyphen{}regular value is often 0
because no non\sphinxhyphen{}trivial robust ECs survive abstraction (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0011, a modelling fact,
not a solver bug).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Objective Verification}
\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective:multi-objective-verification}}\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Weighted\sphinxhyphen{}sum multi\sphinxhyphen{}objective robust reachability and Pareto frontier tracing on
interval MDPs.


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Given k target label sets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T\_1, ..., T\_k}} (all made absorbing, so each objective is
“the first target hit is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T\_i}}”) and a weight vector \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{w}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi}} maximises

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
w · ( P(reach T\PYGZus{}1), ..., P(reach T\PYGZus{}k) )
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
over controller policies, with nature adversarial (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound pess}}, default) or
cooperative (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound opt}}). The output is the weighted optimum at the initial state
\sphinxstylestrong{and} the per\sphinxhyphen{}objective vector \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P(reach T\_i)}} achieved by the weight\sphinxhyphen{}optimal policy —
one achievable point on the (robust) Pareto frontier. With no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}weights}} argument and
exactly two objectives, the weight simplex is swept
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{λ ∈ \{0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1\}}}) to trace the frontier.


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The achievable set of a multi\sphinxhyphen{}objective MDP is convex, so its Pareto frontier is traced
by the weighted\sphinxhyphen{}sum optima over the weight simplex:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Etessami, Kwiatkowska, Vardi, Yannakakis, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Objective Model Checking of Markov
Decision Processes}, TACAS 2007 (convexity; memoryless\sphinxhyphen{}randomised strategies
suffice; ε\sphinxhyphen{}approximable Pareto curve).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Forejt, Kwiatkowska, Norman, Parker, Qu, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Quantitative Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Objective Verification
for Probabilistic Systems}, TACAS 2011 (the PRISM implementation this parallels).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Implementation (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solve::multiReach}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.\{h,cpp\}}}): the robust VI is the
ordinary O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization backup with the value promoted to a vector and scalarised
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vv{[}i{]} = Σ\_j w\_j V\_j{[}to{]}}}); the policy recorded at the weighted optimum is then
evaluated per objective.


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective:cli-examples-validated}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_demo}} point MDP offers action A with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(P(F t1), P(F t2)) = (0.9, 0.1)}} and
action B with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0.2, 0.8)}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sweep the weight simplex (2 objectives) — traces the Pareto frontier}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/multi\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }multi\PYG{+w}{ }t1,t2
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pareto  bound=pess  state=0  weights=0,1        objectives=0.2,0.8  weighted=0.8}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pareto  bound=pess  state=0  weights=0.25,0.75  objectives=0.2,0.8  weighted=0.65}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pareto  bound=pess  state=0  weights=0.5,0.5    objectives=0.9,0.1  weighted=0.5}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pareto  bound=pess  state=0  weights=0.75,0.25  objectives=0.9,0.1  weighted=0.7}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pareto  bound=pess  state=0  weights=1,0        objectives=0.9,0.1  weighted=0.9}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} One point for an explicit weight vector (required for k \PYGZgt{} 2 objectives)}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/multi\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }multi\PYG{+w}{ }t1,t2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}weights\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.5,0.5
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pareto  bound=pess  state=0  weights=0.5,0.5  objectives=0.9,0.1  weighted=0.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The sweep recovers exactly the two Pareto vertices \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0.9, 0.1)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(0.2, 0.8)}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_demo.ref.json}}).


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective:peer-tools-and-validation}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Storm}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi(Pmax=?{[}F t1{]}, Pmax=?{[}F t2{]})}} reports “2 Pareto optimal points” on
the same model, matching IMPaCT’s vertices; the corners match Storm’s
single\sphinxhyphen{}objective \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmax=?{[}F t1{]} = 0.9}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmax=?{[}F t2{]} = 0.8}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM}: supports \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi(...)}} Pareto queries — non\sphinxhyphen{}interval models only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IntervalMDP.jl}: no multi\sphinxhyphen{}objective support.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multi\sphinxhyphen{}objective on \sphinxstylestrong{interval} MDPs is IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}only (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} \S{}1b,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}}); peers were compared on the degenerate (point) model.


\subsection{Robust\sphinxhyphen{}Pareto semantics}
\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective:robust-pareto-semantics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For interval models the reported point is what the weight\sphinxhyphen{}optimal policy \sphinxstylestrong{guarantees
robustly per objective}: nature is re\sphinxhyphen{}resolved adversarially for each objective
evaluation. This is a sound achievable point; the fully convex robust\sphinxhyphen{}Pareto set under
a \sphinxstyleemphasis{single} adversarial nature across all objectives is a documented refinement
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ROADMAP\_UPGRADES.md}} \S{}3, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_demo.ref.json}}).


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/multiobjective:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Objectives are \sphinxstylestrong{reachability probabilities only} — reward objectives are a planned
refinement (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ROADMAP\_UPGRADES.md}} \S{}3).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The automatic sweep works for exactly 2 objectives; for k \textgreater{} 2 supply \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}weights}}
vectors yourself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Weighted\sphinxhyphen{}sum scalarisation enumerates the \sphinxstyleemphasis{vertices} of the Pareto frontier;
points on non\sphinxhyphen{}vertex faces are convex combinations of the reported vertices
(randomised policies), not printed explicitly.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{CTMCs and CSL Time\sphinxhyphen{}Bounded Reachability}
\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl:ctmcs-and-csl-time-bounded-reachability}}\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Continuous\sphinxhyphen{}time Markov chains (CTMCs), CSL time\sphinxhyphen{}bounded reachability \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P(F\textless{}=t goal)}},
and the interval (uncertain\sphinxhyphen{}rate) CTMC extension unique to IMPaCT.


\subsection{Model class}
\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl:model-class}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A CTMC is written in the plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} format where each state has a \sphinxstylestrong{single action}
whose entries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to:r:r}} are transition \sphinxstylestrong{rates} (not probabilities; no self rate). An
\sphinxstylestrong{interval CTMC} uses rate intervals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to:rlo:rhi}} — uncertain rates. The entries are
interpreted as rates only by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csl}} property; see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/formats::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{File Formats and Converters}}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} ctmc\PYGZus{}demo.imdp: s0 \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rate 1\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} s1 (absorbing goal); P(F\PYGZlt{}=t goal) = 1 \PYGZhy{} e\PYGZca{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZhy{}t\PYGZcb{}
states 2
init 0
label goal 1
tran 0 0 1:1:1
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csl LABEL \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}time t}} returns the per\sphinxhyphen{}state probability of reaching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LABEL}} within
continuous time \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t}} (goal states made absorbing). For an interval CTMC, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound pess}}
resolves the uncertain rates adversarially per uniformisation step (sound lower CSL
bound) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound opt}} cooperatively (sound upper bound) — the three\sphinxhyphen{}valued CSL
reading of Katoen et al.


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Uniformisation + Fox\sphinxhyphen{}Glynn} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/ctmc.\{h,cpp\}}}): Jensen’s uniformisation builds the
embedded DTMC \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P = I + Q/Λ}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Λ}} = max exit rate; the time\sphinxhyphen{}bounded value is the
Poisson\sphinxhyphen{}weighted transient of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}}, with the Poisson weights computed by the numerically
stable Fox\sphinxhyphen{}Glynn truncation. For interval rates, the uniformised chain is an interval
DTMC whose step distributions are resolved by O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
C. Baier, B. Haverkort, H. Hermanns, J.\sphinxhyphen{}P. Katoen, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Model\sphinxhyphen{}Checking Algorithms for
Continuous\sphinxhyphen{}Time Markov Chains}, IEEE Trans. Software Eng. 29(6):524\sphinxhyphen{}541, 2003
(DOI 10.1109/TSE.2003.1205180).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
B. L. Fox, P. W. Glynn, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Computing Poisson probabilities}, CACM 31(4):440\sphinxhyphen{}445, 1988
(DOI 10.1145/42404.42409).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interval CTMC: Katoen, Klink, Leucker, Wolf, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Three\sphinxhyphen{}Valued Abstraction for CTMCs},
CAV 2007 (DOI 10.1007/978\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}540\sphinxhyphen{}73368\sphinxhyphen{}3\_37); Badings, Jansen, Junges, Stoelinga,
Volk, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Sampling\sphinxhyphen{}Based Verification of CTMCs with Uncertain Rates}, CAV 2022
(arXiv:2205.08300).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Steady\sphinxhyphen{}state analysis of a CTMC reuses the LRA machinery: the uniformised DTMC has the
same stationary distribution as the CTMC (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/lra-steadystate::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Long\sphinxhyphen{}Run Average and Steady\sphinxhyphen{}State}}}}).


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl:cli-examples-validated}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Point CTMC: P(F\PYGZlt{}=1 goal) = 1 \PYGZhy{} e\PYGZca{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZhy{}1\PYGZcb{} = 0.6321206}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/ctmc\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }csl\PYG{+w}{ }goal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}time\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}.0
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=csl  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0.6321205588  upper=0.6321205588  iters=0}

tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/ctmc\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }csl\PYG{+w}{ }goal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}time\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}.0
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=csl  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0.8646647168  upper=0.8646647168  iters=0}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Interval CTMC (rate in [0.5, 1.5]) — IMPaCT\PYGZhy{}only:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} robust 1\PYGZhy{}e\PYGZca{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZhy{}0.5\PYGZcb{} = 0.3934693, best\PYGZhy{}case 1\PYGZhy{}e\PYGZca{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZhy{}1.5\PYGZcb{} = 0.7768698}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/ctmc\PYGZus{}interval.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }csl\PYG{+w}{ }goal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}time\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}.0\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=csl  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0.3934693403  upper=0.3934693403  iters=0}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=csl  bound=opt   state=0  lower=0.7768698399  upper=0.7768698399  iters=0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl:peer-tools-and-validation}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Point CTMC}: IMPaCT == Storm CSL (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{storm \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}prism ctmc\_demo.sm \sphinxhyphen{}pc \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}prop \textquotesingle{}P=?{[}F\textless{}=t "goal"{]}\textquotesingle{}}}) == the analytic value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1 \sphinxhyphen{} e\textasciicircum{}\{\sphinxhyphen{}t\}}} \sphinxstylestrong{to 10 digits} for
t = 0.5, 1, 2 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctmc\_demo.ref.json}}; the PRISM\sphinxhyphen{}language twin \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctmc\_demo.sm}} ships
alongside the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}}). PRISM supports point\sphinxhyphen{}rate CSL equivalently.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interval CTMC}: Storm and PRISM support point rates only, so the robust values
were validated against the exact analytic bounds above (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ctmc\_interval.ref.json}}) —
\sphinxstylestrong{an IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}only capability} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}}).

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csl}} property covers \sphinxstylestrong{time\sphinxhyphen{}bounded reachability} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P(F\textless{}=t goal)}}; nested CSL
(time\sphinxhyphen{}bounded until with a lower time bound, nested \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}} operators) is not
exposed. Unbounded CSL reachability equals the embedded\sphinxhyphen{}DTMC reachability (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reach}}),
and steady\sphinxhyphen{}state uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The model must be a chain at the CTMC level: one action per state (CTMDPs are not
supported; nondeterminism plus continuous time is the Markov\sphinxhyphen{}automata gap tracked in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}} \S{}B).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The interval\sphinxhyphen{}rate resolution is per uniformisation step (step\sphinxhyphen{}wise adversary), the
standard sound bound of the three\sphinxhyphen{}valued CSL construction; a time\sphinxhyphen{}invariant adversary
could be tighter.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Parametric Region Verification}
\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric:parametric-region-verification}}\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Verify a \sphinxstyleemphasis{parametric} Markov model over a whole parameter region in one solve, by
reducing region verification to robust interval\sphinxhyphen{}MDP reachability (Parameter Lifting).


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Given a Markov model whose transition probabilities are expressions in a parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}}
and a region \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p ∈ {[}lo, hi{]}}}, the lifted interval MDP’s robust \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}pess, opt{]}}}
reachability values \sphinxstylestrong{bound the parametric value over the entire region}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pess  \PYGZlt{}=  min\PYGZus{}\PYGZob{}p in [lo,hi]\PYGZcb{} P\PYGZus{}p(F target)   and   max\PYGZus{}\PYGZob{}p in [lo,hi]\PYGZcb{} P\PYGZus{}p(F target)  \PYGZlt{}=  opt
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bound is \sphinxstylestrong{exact} when each parameter occurs once per transition row, and a
\sphinxstylestrong{sound over\sphinxhyphen{}approximation} otherwise (each parameter \sphinxstyleemphasis{occurrence} is relaxed
independently — precisely the Parameter Lifting relaxation).


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameter Lifting: relax parameter dependencies so each occurrence ranges over the
region independently; the result is an interval MDP, and robust reachability on it
bounds the parametric solution function over the region.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quatmann, Dehnert, Jansen, Junges, Katoen, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Parameter Synthesis for Markov Models:
Faster Than Ever}, ATVA 2016 (DOI 10.1007/978\sphinxhyphen{}3\sphinxhyphen{}319\sphinxhyphen{}46520\sphinxhyphen{}3\_4).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a natural fit: parametric region checking ≡ interval/robust solving, which is
IMPaCT’s native engine (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}} \S{}B). The lifting itself is the standalone
script \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/peers/param\_lift.py}}; the solve is the ordinary
{\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/specifications::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Probabilistic Specifications}}}} machinery.


\subsection{The \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.pimdp}} format}
\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric:the-pimdp-format}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/formats::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{File Formats and Converters}}}}) with two changes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a region directive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{param \textless{}name\textgreater{} \textless{}lo\textgreater{} \textless{}hi\textgreater{}}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tran \textless{}s\textgreater{} \textless{}a\textgreater{} \textless{}to\textgreater{}:\textless{}expr\textgreater{} ...}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}expr\textgreater{}}} is \sphinxstylestrong{affine in the single parameter}:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1\sphinxhyphen{}p}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a*p+b}}.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZsh{} param\PYGZus{}demo.pimdp — P(F target) = p; region p in [0.3, 0.7]
param p 0.3 0.7
states 3
init 0
label target 1
tran 0 0 1:p 2:1\PYGZhy{}p
tran 1 0 1:1
tran 2 0 2:1
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{CLI example (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric:cli-example-validated}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1. Lift the parametric model over its region to an interval MDP}
python3\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/peers/param\PYGZus{}lift.py\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }benchmarks/crosstool/models/param\PYGZus{}demo.pimdp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }/tmp/param\PYGZus{}demo.imdp

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2. Robust reachability on the lifted IMDP = region bounds on P\PYGZus{}p(F target)}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }/tmp/param\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0.3  upper=0.300001  iters=2}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=opt   state=0  lower=0.7  upper=0.700001  iters=2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P\_p(F target) = p}}, so the region \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.3, 0.7{]}}} maps exactly to the value range
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.3, 0.7{]}}} — the lifting is exact because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}} occurs once per row
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{param\_demo.ref.json}}).


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric:peer-tools-and-validation}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Storm} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{storm\sphinxhyphen{}pars}}) is the reference implementation of Parameter Lifting region
checking. In the recorded validation the lifted IMPaCT bounds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.3, 0.7{]}}} were
confirmed against \sphinxstylestrong{Storm corner instantiations} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p=0.3 \(\rightarrow\) 0.3}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p=0.7 \(\rightarrow\) 0.7}}) and
the analytic value (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{param\_demo.ref.json}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{storm\sphinxhyphen{}pars}} itself was not built in the
comparison container — the corners confirm the endpoints, while the lifting covers
the whole region in one interval\sphinxhyphen{}MDP solve).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM} supports parametric models via its param engine (solution functions);
region verification per se is Storm’s feature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IntervalMDP.jl}: no parametric support.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/parametric:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Expressions must be affine in \sphinxstylestrong{one} parameter per transition expression
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{param\_lift.py}}); multi\sphinxhyphen{}parameter models need one \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{param}} region but each edge
expression references a single parameter. Rational\sphinxhyphen{}function transition
probabilities (parametric \sphinxstyleemphasis{solution functions}, Daws ICTAC 2004 state elimination)
are a planned item, not implemented (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}} \S{}B).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When a parameter occurs multiple times in one distribution row, the lifted bound is
sound but not tight (the relaxation decouples the occurrences) — the standard
Parameter Lifting trade\sphinxhyphen{}off; refine by splitting the region.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Region \sphinxstyleemphasis{refinement loops} (automatic splitting until a threshold is decided) are not
provided; run the lift\sphinxhyphen{}and\sphinxhyphen{}solve per subregion yourself.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Orthogonal and Mixture IMDPs}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:orthogonal-and-mixture-imdps}}\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Factored interval MDPs whose transition ambiguity decomposes per state dimension —
IntervalMDP.jl’s scalability representation, now solved natively by IMPaCT.


\subsection{Model class}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:model-class}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxstylestrong{orthogonally\sphinxhyphen{}decoupled IMDP (odIMDP)} has a product state space
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S = S\_1 × ... × S\_n}}; the ambiguity set of each (state, action) factors as a product
of \sphinxstylestrong{per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension marginal interval distributions}. Storing n marginals of size
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|S\_d|}} instead of one joint distribution of size \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Π|S\_d|}} is the memory/compute
scalability feature — and matches the per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension transition bounds IMPaCT’s own
sparse abstraction produces for decoupled dynamics (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/abstraction.cpp}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{mixture IMDP} generalises this: one action is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{mixture} of orthogonal
components, where nature picks both a weight vector within interval weights and each
component’s marginals within theirs.


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reach}} (the only property supported on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.odimdp}} inputs): robust max\sphinxhyphen{}reachability with
the controller maximising and nature choosing factored distributions adversarially
(pess) or cooperatively (opt).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reduction\sphinxhyphen{}order convention (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0022).} The factored ambiguity set is
\sphinxstyleemphasis{reduction\sphinxhyphen{}order sensitive}: nature’s inner marginal choices may condition on the
destination coordinates already realised by the outer dimensions (per\sphinxhyphen{}prefix
rectangular semantics), so different reduction orders define different nature classes
and can give different pessimistic values. IMPaCT reduces \sphinxstylestrong{dimension 1 innermost}
(then 2, …, n outermost) — exactly IntervalMDP.jl’s convention (its
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{state\_action\_bellman}} reduces dimension 1 first per combination of the remaining
coordinates). When citing or comparing factored values, always state the convention.


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Robust Bellman backup by \sphinxstylestrong{recursive per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/odimdp.\{h,cpp\}}}): reduce the value hyper\sphinxhyphen{}rectangle one dimension at a time,
optimising the dim\sphinxhyphen{}d marginal per prefix of the outer destination coordinates. For
mixtures: per\sphinxhyphen{}component factored O\sphinxhyphen{}max, then O\sphinxhyphen{}max over the interval mixture weights.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mathiesen, Haesaert, Laurenti, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Scalable control synthesis for stochastic systems
via structural IMDP abstractions}, arXiv:2411.11803 (odIMDP and mixture ambiguity
sets).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Givan, Leach, Dean, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Bounded\sphinxhyphen{}parameter MDPs}, AIJ 2000 (the per\sphinxhyphen{}marginal inner
solve).

\end{itemize}


\subsection{The \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.odimdp}} format}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:the-odimdp-format}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
odimdp
dims n1 n2 ...                        \PYGZsh{} per\PYGZhy{}dimension sizes; states linearised, dim 0 fastest
init s
label NAME s ...
otran  \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}d\PYGZgt{} to:lo:hi ...       \PYGZsh{} dim\PYGZhy{}d marginal of action a (single component)
mtran  \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}k\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}d\PYGZgt{} to:lo:hi ...   \PYGZsh{} dim\PYGZhy{}d marginal of mixture component k
mweight \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} k:lo:hi ...           \PYGZsh{} interval mixture weights over components
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/models/od\_demo.odimdp}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mix\_demo.odimdp}} for complete
commented examples.


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:cli-examples-validated}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Orthogonal IMDP, 2x2 product space, interval marginals per dimension}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/od\PYGZus{}demo.odimdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0.3714280537  upper=0.3714280537  iters=17}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=opt   state=0  lower=0.8536579107  upper=0.8536579107  iters=20}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Mixture\PYGZhy{}of\PYGZhy{}orthogonal IMDP with interval mixture weights}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/mix\PYGZus{}demo.odimdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0.47567519    upper=0.47567519    iters=17}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=opt   state=0  lower=0.9619447054  upper=0.9619447054  iters=19}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
(Default \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}eps 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6}} VI; the converged references are 0.3714285709 / 0.8536585360 and
0.4756756752 / 0.9619450314.)


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:peer-tools-and-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The oracle is \sphinxstylestrong{IntervalMDP.jl} on the \sphinxstyleemphasis{identical} models:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OrthogonalIntervalMarkovDecisionProcess}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/peers/odimdp\_oracle.jl}})
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MixtureIntervalMarkovDecisionProcess}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/mixture\_oracle.jl}}), with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{InfiniteTimeReachability}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pessimistic/Optimistic × Maximize}}. At tight
thresholds \sphinxstylestrong{IMPaCT matches IntervalMDP.jl to 10 digits in both senses} on both
models (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{od\_demo.ref.json}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}}). PRISM and Storm have no factored
IMDP representation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first implementation reduced the \sphinxstyleemphasis{highest} dimension innermost and disagreed with
IntervalMDP.jl in the pessimistic sense (0.3478 vs 0.3714 on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{od\_demo}}) while agreeing
optimistically — the discriminating experiment that pinned the convention
(ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0022).


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/odimdp:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reach}} is dispatched for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.odimdp}} inputs (no safety/ω\sphinxhyphen{}regular/reward on the
factored representation yet); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}eps}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}state}} apply as usual.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.odimdp}} solver runs plain VI with residual stopping (single value reported as
both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{upper}}), not the certified OVI bracket of the joint solver.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool factored values are only comparable under a pinned reduction order
(ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0022).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Exact Rational Solving}
\label{\detokenize{manual/exact:exact-rational-solving}}\label{\detokenize{manual/exact::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reach \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact}}: robust reachability computed \sphinxstylestrong{exactly over the rationals}, with a
machine\sphinxhyphen{}checked fixpoint certificate — including on \sphinxstyleemphasis{interval} models, where the peer
tools’ exact modes do not work at all.


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/exact:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exact robust value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P(F target)}} at one queried state, as a fraction (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2/5}}),
for a point or interval \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} model (decimal inputs are parsed exactly as
fractions). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound pess}} is adversarial nature, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opt}} cooperative. The result line
reports the fraction, a decimal approximation, the policy\sphinxhyphen{}iteration round count, and
whether the \sphinxstylestrong{certificate} passed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
result  prop=reach\PYGZhy{}exact  bound=pess  state=0  exact=2/5  approx=0.4  certified=yes  iters=2
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rationals are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{long long}} numerator/denominator with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_int128}} intermediates and gcd
normalisation; \sphinxstylestrong{overflow throws} rather than silently losing exactness.


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/exact:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Policy iteration in the Hoffman\sphinxhyphen{}Karp style over the controller policy \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} nature’s
O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization vertex — both spaces are finite because the O\sphinxhyphen{}max vertex depends only on
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{ordering} of the value vector (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/exact.\{h,cpp\}}}):
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Qualitative preprocessing}: compute the exact robust prob\sphinxhyphen{}0 set P0 (the largest
target\sphinxhyphen{}free set nature can confine the play to) and pin it to 0.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exact policy evaluation}: rational Gaussian elimination on the induced point
chain (chain\sphinxhyphen{}level unreachability pinned to 0).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Improvement}: better controller action / nature vertex by exact O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization
(which is division\sphinxhyphen{}free — sort plus additive mass assignment — so nature’s vertex
is computed exactly); repeat until stable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Certificate}: verify the result is an exact fixpoint of the robust Bellman
operator. Fixpoints vanishing on P0 are unique for reachability, so the certified
fixpoint \sphinxstyleemphasis{is} the robust value.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Literature (from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/exact.h}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iyengar, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Robust Dynamic Programming}, Math. OR 2005, \S{}3.3 (robust policy
iteration).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Puterman, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Markov Decision Processes}, 1994, Ch. 6\sphinxhyphen{}7 (classical policy iteration).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Givan, Leach, Dean, AIJ 2000 (division\sphinxhyphen{}free O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uniqueness of the pinned fixpoint: Baier \& Katoen, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Principles of Model Checking},
Thm 10.100ff; Haddad \& Monmege, TCS 2018 (interval/MDP setting).

\end{itemize}


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/exact:cli-examples-validated}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Point chain: exact 1/4 (== PRISM \PYGZhy{}exact == Storm \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}exact)}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/chain\PYGZus{}point.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}exact\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach\PYGZhy{}exact  bound=pess  state=0  exact=1/4  approx=0.25  certified=yes  iters=2}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} INTERVAL models — exact robust values, certified (peers cannot do this at all)}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/choice\PYGZus{}interval.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}exact\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach\PYGZhy{}exact  bound=pess  state=0  exact=2/5  approx=0.4  certified=yes  iters=2}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach\PYGZhy{}exact  bound=opt   state=0  exact=1/2  approx=0.5  certified=yes  iters=2}

tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/fork\PYGZus{}interval.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}exact\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach\PYGZhy{}exact  bound=pess  state=0  exact=2/5  approx=0.4  certified=yes  iters=3}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach\PYGZhy{}exact  bound=opt   state=0  exact=3/5  approx=0.6  certified=yes  iters=2}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Point vs interval, and the peers}
\label{\detokenize{manual/exact:point-vs-interval-and-the-peers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PRISM’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}exact}} and Storm’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact}} support \sphinxstylestrong{point models only} — verified
empirically: both error on interval inputs (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}} \S{}B). On the point
chain all three agree on exactly \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1/4}}. The certified interval values \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2/5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1/2}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3/5}} above make \sphinxstylestrong{exact robust interval solving unique to IMPaCT}.


\subsection{Infeasible\sphinxhyphen{}row strictness (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0023)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/exact:infeasible-row-strictness-issue-0023}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Exact arithmetic makes model\sphinxhyphen{}validity checking unavoidable. Rows whose upper bounds
sum to slightly below 1 (e.g. truncated decimals like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.999997}} in the
IntervalMDP.jl\sphinxhyphen{}shipped robot model) admit \sphinxstylestrong{no} probability distribution, and exact
mode aborts:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/multiObj\PYGZus{}robotIMDP.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}exact
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} exact error: exact: infeasible interval row (sum hi \PYGZlt{} 1)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Floating\sphinxhyphen{}point solvers (IMPaCT’s own O\sphinxhyphen{}max, and evidently PRISM / Storm /
IntervalMDP.jl) silently tolerate such rows, effectively giving the missing \textasciitilde{}3e\sphinxhyphen{}6 mass
to the highest\sphinxhyphen{}value successor — so cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool comparisons on such models compare
\sphinxstyleemphasis{silent\sphinxhyphen{}repair conventions}. The strict abort is deliberate (the same strictness that
certifies fixpoints certifies input sanity); a possible future \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact\sphinxhyphen{}repair}} option
would scale the upper bounds to feasibility and report the perturbation (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0023).


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/exact:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact}} supports the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reach}} property only (safety = 1 − reach to avoid can be
obtained by complementing by hand; other properties are floating\sphinxhyphen{}point only).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fixed\sphinxhyphen{}width rationals: models whose exact solution needs very large
numerators/denominators throw on overflow rather than approximating (switch to the
floating\sphinxhyphen{}point solver in that case).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Values are reported for a single queried state (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}state}}, default init), not the
whole vector.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Statistical Model Checking}
\label{\detokenize{manual/smc:statistical-model-checking}}\label{\detokenize{manual/smc::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Monte\sphinxhyphen{}Carlo simulation of point Markov chains: probability estimation with confidence
intervals, and sequential hypothesis testing (SPRT) for threshold queries.


\subsection{What is computed}
\label{\detokenize{manual/smc:what-is-computed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smc LABEL}} samples paths of a \sphinxstylestrong{point} chain (one action per state, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lo == hi}}) from
the initial state (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}state S}}) and estimates the step\sphinxhyphen{}bounded reachability
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P(F\textless{}=horizon LABEL)}}; paths stop early in absorbing states. Default horizon is 1000
(override with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}horizon k}}), default sample count 100000 (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}samples N}}). The
estimate line reports:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{estimate}} — fraction of sampled paths that hit the target;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wilson95={[}lo,hi{]}}} — the Wilson 95\% confidence interval;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chernoff\_eps}} — the APMC / Chernoff\sphinxhyphen{}Hoeffding half\sphinxhyphen{}width ε such that
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P(|estimate − p| \textgreater{}= ε) \textless{}= δ}} with δ = 0.05.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}threshold p}}, a second line gives the \sphinxstylestrong{Wald SPRT} verdict for
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{H0: P \textgreater{}= θ+δ}} vs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{H1: P \textless{}= θ−δ}} with error bounds α = β = 0.01 and indifference
region 2δ (δ = 0.01): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{accept(P\textgreater{}=theta)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reject(P\textless{}theta)}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{undecided}} (sample
budget exhausted, capped at 10× \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}samples}}), plus the number of samples the
sequential test actually used.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Seeds are fixed (estimation seed 20260702, SPRT seed 20260703), so runs are
reproducible.


\subsection{Algorithm and literature}
\label{\detokenize{manual/smc:algorithm-and-literature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Plain Monte\sphinxhyphen{}Carlo path sampling with rigorous statistics (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/smc.\{h,cpp\}}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Younes, Simmons, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Probabilistic Verification of Discrete Event Systems Using
Acceptance Sampling}, CAV 2002 (SPRT\sphinxhyphen{}based statistical model checking).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hérault, Lassaigne, Magniette, Peyronnet, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Approximate Probabilistic Model
Checking}, VMCAI 2004 (APMC: Chernoff\sphinxhyphen{}Hoeffding sample bounds).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wald, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses}, Annals of Mathematical
Statistics 16(2), 1945 (the SPRT itself).

\end{itemize}


\subsection{CLI examples (validated)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/smc:cli-examples-validated}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bounded\_demo}} reaches the goal with probability \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1 − 0.5\textasciicircum{}3 = 0.875}} within 3 steps:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Estimation with Wilson 95\PYGZpc{} CI and Chernoff half\PYGZhy{}width}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/bounded\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }smc\PYG{+w}{ }goal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}horizon\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=smc  state=0  estimate=0.87471  wilson95=[0.8726437795,0.876747433]}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}         chernoff\PYGZus{}eps=0.004294694083  samples=100000}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} SPRT: is P \PYGZgt{}= 0.8?  (true: 0.875 \PYGZgt{}= 0.8) — accepted after 570 samples}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/bounded\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }smc\PYG{+w}{ }goal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}horizon\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}threshold\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.8
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=smc\PYGZhy{}sprt  threshold=0.8   verdict=accept(P\PYGZgt{}=theta)  samples=570}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} SPRT: is P \PYGZgt{}= 0.95? (false) — rejected after 199 samples}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/bounded\PYGZus{}demo.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }smc\PYG{+w}{ }goal\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}horizon\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}threshold\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.95
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=smc\PYGZhy{}sprt  threshold=0.95  verdict=reject(P\PYGZlt{}theta)   samples=199}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Wilson interval \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.87264, 0.87675{]}}} contains the analytic 0.875, and the SPRT
decides both directions correctly with two to three orders of magnitude fewer samples
than the fixed\sphinxhyphen{}size estimate.


\subsection{Peer tools and validation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/smc:peer-tools-and-validation}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}sim}} (its discrete\sphinxhyphen{}event simulator, also DTMC\sphinxhyphen{}only for probability
estimation). On the same query PRISM \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}sim}} returned \sphinxstylestrong{0.87479} vs IMPaCT’s
\sphinxstylestrong{0.87471} — both within their confidence intervals of the analytic 0.875
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}} \S{}B).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Storm}: has a simulation\sphinxhyphen{}based engine for point models.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IntervalMDP.jl}: no statistical model checking.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Limitations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/smc:limitations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Point chains only}: the model must have one action per state with degenerate
intervals; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smc}} throws otherwise. MDP scheduler sampling is future work — the same
scope as PRISM’s simulator (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/smc.h}}). There is no meaningful SMC semantics for
\sphinxstyleemphasis{interval} uncertainty without fixing a nature policy; use the robust numeric
solvers for intervals.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The property is step\sphinxhyphen{}bounded reachability only (choose \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}horizon}} large enough to
approximate unbounded reachability on absorbing chains; paths that reach an
absorbing non\sphinxhyphen{}target state stop early, so a large horizon is cheap there).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Statistical guarantees are confidence statements, not the sound \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}lower, upper{]}}}
brackets of the numeric engines — use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smc}} for quick estimation or very large
chains, and the numeric solvers for certified values.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Solver Engines}
\label{\detokenize{manual/engines:solver-engines}}\label{\detokenize{manual/engines::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT ships a toolbox of infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon convergence methods. This page explains
what each computes, when each is sound, and which to choose.


\subsection{The three iteration methods (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{IterationMethod}})}
\label{\detokenize{manual/engines:the-three-iteration-methods-iterationmethod}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The abstraction\sphinxhyphen{}side synthesis API (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMDP::setIterationMethod}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/IMDP.h}}) selects
among three methods for infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon robust value iteration; the same solvers back
the CLI (the dense SYCL path dispatches infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon OVI through the shared CPU
solver \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.cpp}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IntervalIteration}}} (dense\sphinxhyphen{}path default) — sound interval iteration: iterate the
robust Bellman operator from 0 (lower) and from 1 (upper), stop when
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|upper − lower| \textless{} eps}}. A rigorous two\sphinxhyphen{}sided bracket (Baier et al., CAV 2017;
Haddad \& Monmege, TCS 2018), but on weakly\sphinxhyphen{}contracting / end\sphinxhyphen{}component models the
gap can close slowly or never (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0003).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ValueIteration}}} — what the peers (PRISM / Storm / IntervalMDP.jl) run by
default: plain VI with \sphinxstyleemphasis{residual} stopping. Far fewer sweeps and converges even with
end components (the from\sphinxhyphen{}0 iterate tends to the least fixed point = the robust
value), but the residual stop is \sphinxstylestrong{not} a sound two\sphinxhyphen{}sided certificate.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OptimisticVI}}} (CLI default) — optimistic value iteration (Hartmanns \& Kaminski,
CAV 2020): VI from below for the lower bound plus a \sphinxstyleemphasis{verified inductive} upper bound
— a candidate \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{U}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F(U) \textless{}= U}} implies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{V* \textless{}= U}} by Knaster\sphinxhyphen{}Tarski. A sound
two\sphinxhyphen{}sided certificate that needs \sphinxstylestrong{no end\sphinxhyphen{}component handling}. The from\sphinxhyphen{}below phase
is \sphinxstylestrong{topological Gauss\textendash{}Seidel} (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0010, resolved 2026\sphinxhyphen{}07\sphinxhyphen{}02): the support graph
is decomposed into strongly connected components, iterated to convergence in reverse
topological order with successor components already fixed (Dai, Mausam, Weld,
Goldsmith, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Topological Value Iteration Algorithms}, JAIR 42:181\textendash{}209, 2011, DOI
10.1613/jair.3390; acyclic states take a single pass), with in\sphinxhyphen{}place Gauss\textendash{}Seidel
sweeps (Puterman, 1994, \S{}6.3.3). Both preserve monotone convergence from below to the
same least fixpoint, and the inductive certificate is verified globally afterwards,
so soundness is independent of the sweep schedule. Measured effect: the ARCH \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BA}}
robust safety solve at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}eps 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6}} went from \sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}180 s (timeout) to 7.8 s} (\textgreater{}23×),
with all reference values bit\sphinxhyphen{}identical.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_solve}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}method ovi}} (default) selects \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solve::Method::OptimisticVI}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}method mec}} selects \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{solve::Method::MECCollapse}} (interval iteration after
support\sphinxhyphen{}graph maximal\sphinxhyphen{}end\sphinxhyphen{}component collapse).


\subsection{The nature trap (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0003)}
\label{\detokenize{manual/engines:the-nature-trap-issue-0003}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pessimistic interval iteration with \sphinxstyleemphasis{support\sphinxhyphen{}graph} MEC collapse does not converge on
\sphinxstylestrong{nature\sphinxhyphen{}confinable end components}: nature can confine the play in a set by sending
a leaving edge to its lower bound 0, creating a non\sphinxhyphen{}unique fixpoint that the upper
iterate never leaves. Minimal example (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/models/naturetrap.imdp}}):
state 0 stays with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.5, 1.0{]}}} or leaves with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.0, 0.5{]}}} — nature zeroes the
leaving edge, so the true robust value at 0 is \sphinxstylestrong{0}, but the support graph sees no
MEC and the classic upper bound sticks at 1.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} OVI (default): converges to the true robust value 0 with a certified bracket}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/naturetrap.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}method\PYG{+w}{ }ovi
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=pess  state=0  lower=0  upper=1e\PYGZhy{}06  iters=2}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} MEC collapse in the OPTIMISTIC sense: valid and fast (support EC = optimistic EC)}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/models/naturetrap.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{+w}{ }target\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }opt\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}method\PYG{+w}{ }mec
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} result  prop=reach  bound=opt  state=0  lower=0.9999980927  upper=1  iters=20}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
OVI resolving the nature trap is why it is the default; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MECCollapse}} remains valid
for point MDPs and for the optimistic sense (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.h}}).

\subsection{Performance notes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/engines:performance-notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0010} (resolved 2026\sphinxhyphen{}07\sphinxhyphen{}02): OVI’s from\sphinxhyphen{}below iterate mixed slowly on large,
strongly\sphinxhyphen{}recurrent IMDPs (the ARCH \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BA}} case needed \textgreater{}180 s at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eps 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6}}). Resolved
by the topological Gauss\textendash{}Seidel from\sphinxhyphen{}below phase described above: BA robust safety at
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eps 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6}} now solves in \sphinxstylestrong{7.8 s} with identical values. For stubborn cases the
older remedies remain available: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}method mec}} or a looser \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}eps}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0017} (resolved): the SYCL dense VI was slow versus Storm/IntervalMDP.jl on
recurrent IMDPs; the infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon dense path now dispatches through the shared
CPU OVI solver (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMDP::infiniteHorizonOVIDispatch}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/IMDP.h}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All methods share the same O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization inner solve, so per\sphinxhyphen{}sweep cost is
identical; they differ only in sweep counts and certification.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Soundness summary}
\label{\detokenize{manual/engines:soundness-summary}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OptimisticVI}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IntervalIteration}} return certified \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}lower, upper{]}}} with
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gap \textless{}= 2*eps}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ValueIteration}} returns an uncertified estimate. The pessimistic
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MECCollapse}} upper bound is \sphinxstyleemphasis{valid} but may not converge on interval nature traps —
the CLI defaults protect you from this; only override \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}method}} in the situations
listed above.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{File Formats and Converters}
\label{\detokenize{manual/formats:file-formats-and-converters}}\label{\detokenize{manual/formats::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The neutral exchange formats read by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_solve}}, and the converters that move models
between IMPaCT and PRISM / Storm / IntervalMDP.jl.


\subsection{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} — explicit (interval) MDP}
\label{\detokenize{manual/formats:imdp-explicit-interval-mdp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Whitespace\sphinxhyphen{}separated text, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#}} comments, blank lines ignored (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/imdp\_io.h}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
states \PYGZlt{}N\PYGZgt{}                       \PYGZsh{} required, first
init \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{}                         \PYGZsh{} optional, default 0
label \PYGZlt{}NAME\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} ...         \PYGZsh{} repeatable; accumulates state sets
reward \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}value\PYGZgt{}               \PYGZsh{} optional; per\PYGZhy{}state reward (expected\PYGZhy{}reward / LRA props)
tran \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}to\PYGZgt{}:\PYGZlt{}lo\PYGZgt{}:\PYGZlt{}hi\PYGZgt{} ...  \PYGZsh{} one line = one action of state \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{}: an interval distribution
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Point MDPs / DTMCs} use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lo == hi}} on every edge.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rewards}: states without a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward}} line have reward 0. Rewards are state\sphinxhyphen{}based.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rates (CTMCs)}: a CTMC is a plain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} whose single action per state carries
transition \sphinxstylestrong{rates} in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to:r:r}} entries (interval rates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to:rlo:rhi}} give an
interval CTMC). The entries are interpreted as rates only by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csl}} property —
see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/ctmc-csl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{CTMCs and CSL Time\sphinxhyphen{}Bounded Reachability}}}}. Example: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/models/ctmc\_demo.imdp}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The parser validates state ranges and rejects unknown directives; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{io::write}}
round\sphinxhyphen{}trips \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{io::parse}}.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.odimdp}} — orthogonal / mixture IMDP}
\label{\detokenize{manual/formats:odimdp-orthogonal-mixture-imdp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Factored per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension marginals over a product state space (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/odimdp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Orthogonal and Mixture IMDPs}}}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
odimdp
dims \PYGZlt{}n1\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}n2\PYGZgt{} ...                     \PYGZsh{} nStates = n1*n2*...; linearised, dim 0 fastest
init \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{}
label \PYGZlt{}NAME\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} ...
otran  \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}d\PYGZgt{} to:lo:hi ...        \PYGZsh{} dim\PYGZhy{}d marginal interval distribution (1 component)
mtran  \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}k\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}d\PYGZgt{} to:lo:hi ...    \PYGZsh{} dim\PYGZhy{}d marginal of mixture component k
mweight \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} k:lo:hi ...            \PYGZsh{} interval mixture weights over components
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{otran}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mtran}} is a \sphinxstylestrong{dimension\sphinxhyphen{}d destination coordinate} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0..dims{[}d{]}\sphinxhyphen{}1}},
not a global state. Examples: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{od\_demo.odimdp}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mix\_demo.odimdp}}.


\subsection{\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{.pimdp}} — parametric MDP}
\label{\detokenize{manual/formats:pimdp-parametric-mdp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} plus a region directive; solved by lifting to an interval MDP (see
{\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/parametric::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Parametric Region Verification}}}}):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
param \PYGZlt{}name\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}lo\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}hi\PYGZgt{}             \PYGZsh{} the parameter region
tran \PYGZlt{}s\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}a\PYGZgt{} \PYGZlt{}to\PYGZgt{}:\PYGZlt{}expr\PYGZgt{} ...       \PYGZsh{} \PYGZlt{}expr\PYGZgt{} affine in ONE parameter: c, p, 1\PYGZhy{}p, a*p+b
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{PRISM\sphinxhyphen{}language subset}
\label{\detokenize{manual/formats:prism-language-subset}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_solve}} also reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.prism}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.pm}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.nm}} files through a PRISM\sphinxhyphen{}language
front\sphinxhyphen{}end (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/prism.h}}) targeting the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Problem}} struct, so both front ends feed
one solver path. Validated: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choice.prism}} gives the identical robust values (0.4 /
0.5) as its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} twin (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choice.prism.ref.json}}).


\subsection{Exporting an abstraction: \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{IMDP::exportIMDP}}}
\label{\detokenize{manual/formats:exporting-an-abstraction-imdp-exportimdp}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The abstraction front end writes its in\sphinxhyphen{}memory interval matrices to the neutral format
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exportIMDP("model.imdp")}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/GPU\_synthesis.cpp}}) — this is how the cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool
comparisons run peers on IMPaCT’s abstractions (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}}). Note: the
export ignores the disturbance dimension (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dim\_w \textgreater{} 0}} prints a warning).

\subsection{Interoperability caveats}
\label{\detokenize{manual/formats:interoperability-caveats}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM zero lower bounds}: fixed positive support graph required; floor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}}
edges first (above).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infeasible rows}: some third\sphinxhyphen{}party models contain rows with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sum(hi) \textless{} 1}}
(truncated decimals); floating\sphinxhyphen{}point solvers silently repair these, IMPaCT’s exact
mode rejects them (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0023, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manual/exact::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Exact Rational Solving}}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Thresholds}: IntervalMDP.jl’s default 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 residual can stop \textasciitilde{}1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 short of the
fixpoint on slowly\sphinxhyphen{}mixing chains — tighten it when comparing digits
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} \S{}4).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

\PYG{+w}{    }src/imdp\PYGZus{}io.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/prism.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/solve.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/omaximization.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }src/graph\PYGZus{}utils.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/omega.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/pctl.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/ltlspec.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }src/ltl\PYGZus{}spot.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/ctmc.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/odimdp.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/smc.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/exact.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}

\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{manual/cli:usage}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output: one tab\sphinxhyphen{}separated \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result}} line per requested bound,
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{result  prop=...  bound=pess|opt  state=S  lower=L  upper=U  iters=N}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi}} prints \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pareto}} lines; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smc}} prints \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smc}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smc\sphinxhyphen{}sprt}} lines; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact}} prints
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exact=}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{approx=}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{certified=}}). Exit codes: 0 success, 1 parse/solve error, 2 usage
error. All examples below use models in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/models/}}.

\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/cli:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usage:}} banner lists the most common properties; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ss}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csl}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{smc}}
and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.odimdp}} modes are dispatched as documented here (source of truth:
the dispatch in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tools/imdp\_solve.cpp}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward}} requires a valid label argument even in discounted mode.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}method mec}} does not converge for the pessimistic sense on interval nature\sphinxhyphen{}traps
(ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0003); keep the OVI default there.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}json}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}trace}} are intended for small models (the web app draws every edge).

\end{itemize}

\section{Tool comparison: IMPaCT vs PRISM vs Storm vs IntervalMDP.jl}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/index:tool-comparison-impact-vs-prism-vs-storm-vs-intervalmdp-jl}}\label{\detokenize{comparison/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section compares IMPaCT against the three peer probabilistic model checkers with
interval\sphinxhyphen{}MDP (IMDP) support, on identical models with aligned robust semantics. It
summarises the repository’s cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool study (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FEATURE\_PARITY.md}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/}}); pairwise pages give more detail per tool:

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-storm::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{IMPaCT vs Storm}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-intervalmdp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{IMPaCT vs IntervalMDP.jl}}}}}

\subsection{Methodology}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/index:methodology}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only IMPaCT \sphinxstyleemphasis{abstracts} a continuous stochastic system into an IMDP; the peers consume a
finite IMDP and only \sphinxstyleemphasis{solve} it. For a fair comparison, IMPaCT exports its abstracted
IMDP to a neutral \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} file, and every tool solves the \sphinxstylestrong{identical model}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} directly (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tools/imdp\_solve}});

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Storm reads a DRN produced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/imdp\_to\_drn.py}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PRISM reads explicit interval \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tra/.sta/.lab}} from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/imdp\_to\_prism\_interval.py}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
IntervalMDP.jl reads the model via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/intervalmdp\_runner.jl}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
One driver runs the whole sweep (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/sweep\_compare.py}}); raw output is in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/sweep\_all.tsv}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sweep\_arch.tsv}}. Robust semantics are aligned
across tools before any number is compared:

\sphinxAtStartPar
All four tools agree on every reachability/safety model. The four ω\sphinxhyphen{}regular models are
IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}only: Storm reports \sphinxstyleemphasis{“LTL with intervals not implemented”}, PRISM \sphinxstyleemphasis{“Computation
not implemented yet”}, and IntervalMDP.jl offers DFA/co\sphinxhyphen{}safe reachability only.
† IntervalMDP.jl’s default 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 threshold stops at 0.894662 (1.2e\sphinxhyphen{}6 low); at a tight
threshold it reaches 0.894663, equal to the others.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On the ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP 2025 abstracted IMDPs (AS, BA, IC, PD, VP — IMPaCT abstracts, the peers
solve the exported model), \sphinxstylestrong{all four tools agree on every robust value}; optimistic
reach also agrees to high precision (e.g. IC\_reach opt ≈ 1.20e\sphinxhyphen{}26 in all four). See the
pairwise pages for the timing breakdowns.


\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool findings}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/index:cross-tool-findings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every observed difference is a documented semantic distinction or a performance
characteristic — no tool returned a different correct value on the same model.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM rejects zero lower bounds.} PRISM 4.8.1 needs a strictly positive support
graph and aborts with \sphinxstyleemphasis{“Transition probability has lower bound of 0”} on abstracted
IMDPs; the sweep floors \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}} edges to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1e\sphinxhyphen{}9,hi{]}}}, so PRISM’s ARCH values are an
ε\sphinxhyphen{}perturbation. PRISM also reports only the initial\sphinxhyphen{}state value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Convergence thresholds must match.} IntervalMDP.jl’s default reachability threshold
(1e\sphinxhyphen{}6) stops \textasciitilde{}1.2e\sphinxhyphen{}6 short of the fixpoint on slowly\sphinxhyphen{}mixing chains. IMPaCT’s OVI
returns the converged value \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} a certified upper bound at the same tolerance.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Storm’s interval rewards ignore the resolution mode.} On interval reward models
Storm returns only the nature\sphinxhyphen{}max value regardless of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}resolution}}
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmin}} unsupported), so robust interval rewards were validated against PRISM’s
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmaxmin/Rmaxmax}} and IntervalMDP.jl instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Factored (odIMDP) semantics are reduction\sphinxhyphen{}order sensitive} (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0022). The robust
value of an orthogonally\sphinxhyphen{}decoupled IMDP depends on which dimension nature resolves
innermost; IMPaCT pins IntervalMDP.jl’s dimension\sphinxhyphen{}1\sphinxhyphen{}innermost convention and then
matches it to 10 digits in both senses.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exact mode surfaces infeasible interval rows} (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0023). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_solve reach \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact}} rejects rows of the IntervalMDP.jl\sphinxhyphen{}shipped robot model whose upper bounds sum
to slightly below 1 (e.g. 0.999997); all floating\sphinxhyphen{}point solvers, IMPaCT’s included,
silently tolerate this and assign the missing \textasciitilde{}3e\sphinxhyphen{}6 mass to the best successor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Optimistic safety is convention\sphinxhyphen{}dependent} across tools (how the cooperative sense
resolves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}} leak edges); the robust value is unambiguous and agrees, so robust is
the headline number everywhere.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Reproducing the comparison}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/index:reproducing-the-comparison}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} in the impact\PYGZus{}work container (repo mounted at /work):}
python3\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/crosstool/peers/sweep\PYGZus{}compare.py\PYG{+w}{ }all\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 4\PYGZhy{}tool sweep \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} TSV}
tools/imdp\PYGZus{}solve\PYG{+w}{ }MODEL.imdp\PYG{+w}{ }reach\PYG{p}{|}safety\PYG{p}{|}buchi\PYG{p}{|}persist\PYG{p}{|}patrol\PYG{+w}{ }LABEL\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bound\PYG{+w}{ }both
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Converters and runners live in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/peers/}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tra\_to\_imdp.py}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_to\_drn.py}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_to\_prism\_interval.py}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intervalmdp\_runner.jl}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build\_storm.sh}}). Per\sphinxhyphen{}model reference values with measured per\sphinxhyphen{}tool numbers are the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/models/*.ref.json}} files; the IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}side benchmark log is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/RESULTS.md}}; design decisions and discrepancies are filed under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{issues/}}.

\section{IMPaCT vs PRISM}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-prism:impact-vs-prism}}\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-prism::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://www.prismmodelchecker.org/}{PRISM} (compared at version 4.8.1, official Linux
binary) is the classic probabilistic model checker: PRISM\sphinxhyphen{}language models, full
PCTL*/LTL/CSL on DTMCs/CTMCs/MDPs, and — since v4.8 (2024) — interval MDPs. It
auto\sphinxhyphen{}detects \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Type: IMDP}} on explicit models and solves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pmaxmin/Pmaxmax=?{[}F ...{]}}},
which is exactly IMPaCT’s robust/optimistic reachability.
