\subsection{Same results on shared models}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-prism:same-results-on-shared-models}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All values below are from live runs recorded in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TOOL\_COMPARISONS.md}} and the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/models/*.ref.json}} measured blocks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interval reference models.} PRISM reproduces every interval reference value exactly:
chain\_point 0.25, safety\_point 0.72, choice\_interval 0.40/0.50, fork\_interval 0.40/0.60.
On the 207\sphinxhyphen{}state \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multiObj\_robotIMDP}}, PRISM returns 0.8946624 (pess) — agreeing with
IMPaCT/Storm’s 0.8946630 to \textasciitilde{}1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 at default tolerances — and 1.0 (opt).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PRISM\sphinxhyphen{}language front end.} IMPaCT parses a PRISM\sphinxhyphen{}language subset directly:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choice.prism}} and the equivalent \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{choice\_interval.imdp}} solve to identical values
(pess 0.4 / opt 0.5) through one solver path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Robust rewards.} On \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward\_chain}} (interval MDP with rewards), IMPaCT’s reachability
reward is pess 3.0 / opt 4.999999 against PRISM’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmaxmin}} 3.000000002 / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmaxmax}}
4.999996 — the analytic values are 3 and 5. PRISM is the oracle here because Storm’s
interval rewards ignore the resolution mode.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Exact arithmetic, 1/4.} On the point chain, IMPaCT’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_solve reach \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exact}}
returns exactly 1/4, matching PRISM \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}exact}} (and Storm’s exact mode). On \sphinxstyleemphasis{interval}
models IMPaCT certifies exact robust values (2/5, 1/2, 3/5 on the reference models)
where PRISM errors — its exact engine is point\sphinxhyphen{}only (verified).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Statistical model checking.} IMPaCT’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_solve smc}} estimate 0.87471 (Wilson CI
containing the analytic 0.875) matches PRISM \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}sim}} 0.87479 on the same point chain.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ARCH abstracted IMDPs.} After flooring (below), PRISM agrees with the other three
tools on every ARCH robust value (AS/IC/VP reach 0, PD 1.0, BA safety 0, IC\_reach opt
≈ 1.20e\sphinxhyphen{}26).


\subsection{Differences and caveats}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-prism:differences-and-caveats}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Zero lower bounds are rejected.} PRISM needs a fixed, strictly positive support
graph and aborts with \sphinxstyleemphasis{“Transition probability has lower bound of 0”}. Abstracted
IMDPs are full of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}} edges, so the sweep floors them to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1e\sphinxhyphen{}9,hi{]}}} for PRISM
only; its ARCH values are therefore an ε\sphinxhyphen{}perturbation of the true robust value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No robust ω\sphinxhyphen{}regular on intervals.} LTL on interval models fails with \sphinxstyleemphasis{“Computation
not implemented yet”}; the Büchi/persistence/patrol reference models are PRISM\sphinxhyphen{}N/A.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Initial\sphinxhyphen{}state reporting.} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{prism}} reports only the initial\sphinxhyphen{}state value; per\sphinxhyphen{}state
comparisons (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chain\_point}} state 1 = 0.5) need the other tools.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No abstraction front end.} PRISM consumes a finite model; the entire
continuous\sphinxhyphen{}dynamics\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}IMDP phase is IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}only.

\end{itemize}

IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}side cost with no PRISM equivalent, because PRISM cannot perform this phase at
all.

\section{IMPaCT vs Storm}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-storm:impact-vs-storm}}\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-storm::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://www.stormchecker.org/}{Storm} (compared at version 1.13.0, built from source in
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{impact\_work}} container via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/build\_storm.sh}}) is a high\sphinxhyphen{}performance
probabilistic model checker with the broadest model\sphinxhyphen{}class coverage of the peers:
DTMC/CTMC/MDP/MA/POMDP, parametric models (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{storm\sphinxhyphen{}pars}}), DFTs and GSPNs. It solves
interval MDPs with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}resolution robust|cooperative}}, which maps directly to
IMPaCT’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound pess|opt}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On the shared interval reference models and the ARCH abstracted IMDPs, Storm agrees with
IMPaCT on every robust value (multiObj\_robotIMDP pess 0.8946629814 vs IMPaCT
0.8946629826; optimistic reach agrees to high precision, e.g. IC\_reach opt ≈ 1.20e\sphinxhyphen{}26).


\subsection{Differences and caveats}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-storm:differences-and-caveats}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interval rewards ignore the resolution mode.} On \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward\_chain}} Storm returns only
the nature\sphinxhyphen{}max reward 4.999996 (= the optimistic value) regardless of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}resolution}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Rmin}} is unsupported — so robust interval rewards
were cross\sphinxhyphen{}validated against PRISM and IntervalMDP.jl instead.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No robust ω\sphinxhyphen{}regular / LRA on intervals.} Storm refuses LTL on interval models
(\sphinxstyleemphasis{“We have not yet implemented LTL with intervals”},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SparseMdpPrctlModelChecker.cpp:239}}) and likewise interval LRA; those capabilities
are IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Point\sphinxhyphen{}only exact and CSL.} Storm’s exact engine and CSL operate on point models;
IMPaCT additionally certifies exact robust values on interval models and solves
interval CTMCs (uncertain rates), which Storm does not support.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No abstraction front end.} Storm consumes DRN/PRISM/JANI models; the
continuous\sphinxhyphen{}dynamics\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}IMDP phase is IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}only.

\end{itemize}

IMPaCT’s finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon robust VI is competitive or faster (BA 0.27 s vs Storm’s
5.86 s + 6.05 s build), and its pure\sphinxhyphen{}VI mode beats Storm on VP (0.59 s vs 1.35 s) and
PD (1.34\textendash{}1.36 s vs \textasciitilde{}8.3 s). Honest flip side: in the later sweep re\sphinxhyphen{}run
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sweep\_arch.tsv}}), Storm’s end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end times on several ARCH models are the best of all
four tools (VP 0.04 s, AS 0.05 s, vs IMPaCT 1.8 s / 0.4 s) — and the abstraction that
produced these IMDPs (e.g. AS 27 s dense / 0.11 s sparse) is an IMPaCT\sphinxhyphen{}side cost Storm
never pays because it cannot abstract.

\section{IMPaCT vs IntervalMDP.jl}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-intervalmdp:impact-vs-intervalmdp-jl}}\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-intervalmdp::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/Zinoex/IntervalMDP.jl}{IntervalMDP.jl} (compared at version 0.6.0 on
Julia 1.10) is a Julia library dedicated to interval MDPs: robust value iteration built
on O\sphinxhyphen{}maximization — the same inner solve IMPaCT uses — with CUDA acceleration and
factored (orthogonal and mixture) IMDP representations for scalability. Of the three
peers it is semantically closest to IMPaCT: both solve \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pessimistic/Optimistic × Maximize}} queries, which map one\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}one to IMPaCT’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bound pess/opt}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
sound bracket {[}0.8946629826, 0.8946629838{]}
\sphinxbeforeendvarwidth
\end{varwidth}%
\\
\sphinxbottomrule
\end{tabulary}
\sphinxtableafterendhook\par
\sphinxattableend\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The values agree to \textasciitilde{}1e\sphinxhyphen{}10 once thresholds match. The apparent 1.2e\sphinxhyphen{}6 gap at defaults is
purely IntervalMDP.jl’s 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 residual threshold terminating short of the fixpoint on
this slowly\sphinxhyphen{}mixing chain — a methodological note, not a disagreement. IMPaCT’s OVI
returns the converged value \sphinxstyleemphasis{and} a certified upper bound already at eps 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6. Both
tools give the optimistic value 1.0 (IMPaCT/Storm 0.9999979999, IntervalMDP.jl/PRISM
0.9999969998).


\subsection{Factored IMDPs: orthogonal and mixture}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-intervalmdp:factored-imdps-orthogonal-and-mixture}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT v2.0 adopts IntervalMDP.jl’s flagship scalability representations, validated
against it as the oracle (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/odimdp\_oracle.jl}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peers/mixture\_oracle.jl}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Orthogonal IMDP} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{od\_demo.odimdp}}): IMPaCT matches
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OrthogonalIntervalMarkovDecisionProcess}} to 10 digits in both senses (state 0 pess
0.3714285709 / opt 0.8536585360; state 1 pess 0.7285714278 / opt 0.9999999995).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mixture IMDP} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mix\_demo.odimdp}}): matches
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MixtureIntervalMarkovDecisionProcess}} to 10 digits both senses (pess 0.4756756752 /
opt 0.9619450314).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reduction\sphinxhyphen{}order semantics (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0022).} The robust value of a factored IMDP
depends on the order in which nature resolves the per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension marginals. IMPaCT’s
first implementation reduced the highest dimension innermost and got pess 0.3478 vs
IntervalMDP.jl’s 0.3714 (optimistic values already matched). Reading
IntervalMDP.jl’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{state\_action\_bellman}} identified its convention — dimension 1
innermost — which IMPaCT now follows; agreement is only meaningful once this
convention is pinned.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Discounted reward} (γ=0.9, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reward\_chain}}): IMPaCT pess 2.8 / opt 4.272726893 vs
IntervalMDP.jl 2.8 / 4.272726893272438 — IntervalMDP.jl is the oracle here since its
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{InfiniteTimeReward}} requires a discount \textless{} 1 and Storm’s interval rewards ignore the
resolution mode.


\subsection{Differences and caveats}
\label{\detokenize{comparison/impact-vs-intervalmdp:differences-and-caveats}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification scope.} IntervalMDP.jl covers reachability, safety, DFA/co\sphinxhyphen{}safe
reachability, discounted reward and exit time; no Büchi/persistence, LRA,
multi\sphinxhyphen{}objective, CTMC or statistical MC. IMPaCT’s robust ω\sphinxhyphen{}regular, LTL, LRA and
multi\sphinxhyphen{}objective queries have no IntervalMDP.jl counterpart.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Optimistic\sphinxhyphen{}safety convention.} On BA’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}} leak edges IntervalMDP.jl’s
cooperative resolution reports opt\sphinxhyphen{}safety ≈ 0.997 where the PRISM/Storm \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1−Pmin}}
encodings give 0 (its BA robust safety, 1.9e\sphinxhyphen{}4, still effectively agrees with the
others’ 0). The robust value is unambiguous; compare that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Thresholds.} Match convergence thresholds before comparing digits (see the robot
example above).

\end{itemize}

second query on the same 4\sphinxhyphen{}state model returns in \textasciitilde{}0.001 s), so small\sphinxhyphen{}model timings
favour the C++ tools. On the 207\sphinxhyphen{}state robot, IntervalMDP.jl solved in 1.2 ms vs
IMPaCT’s \textasciitilde{}10 ms. The sparse\sphinxhyphen{}memory story is shared: IMPaCT’s sparse path is “the
IntervalMDP.jl\sphinxhyphen{}style memory win” — at 125k states the sparse model is \textasciitilde{}255 MB where a
dense matrix would be \textasciitilde{}250 GB, and the 6\sphinxhyphen{}D LM case (dense\sphinxhyphen{}infeasible at \textasciitilde{}96 GB/matrix)
builds and solves at 196 MB.

\section{ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP Benchmarks}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/index:arch-comp-benchmarks}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT ships the ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP 2025 stochastic\sphinxhyphen{}models benchmark suite under
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/}}. Each case abstracts a continuous stochastic system into an
interval MDP (IMDP) and synthesizes a robust controller; the abstracted IMDP is exported
so that peer tools (IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM, Storm) can solve the identical model for
cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation. This section documents each case study, the code used to solve
it, the measured results, and the design decisions behind them.

\subsection{Building and running the dense examples}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/index:building-and-running-the-dense-examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each benchmark directory contains a Makefile that compiles the example against the
IMPaCT sources with AdaptiveCpp (SYCL):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ARCH\PYGZhy{}COMP/2025/AS\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} or BA, VP, IC, PD, PR\PYGZus{}minimal, AV\PYGZus{}minimal, LM}
make
./AS\PYG{+w}{                            }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} executable named after the .cpp file}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Makefile uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{acpp}} with an OpenMP target by default and links NLopt, HDF5, GLPK,
GSL and Armadillo:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{CC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }acpp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} or syclcc (then remove \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}acpp\PYGZhy{}targets=\PYGZdq{}omp\PYGZdq{})}
\PYG{n+nv}{CFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}acpp\PYGZhy{}targets\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}omp\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lnlopt\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}I/usr/include/hdf5/serial\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{         }\PYGZhy{}L/usr/lib/\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}ARCH\PYG{k}{)}\PYGZhy{}linux\PYGZhy{}gnu/hdf5/serial\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lhdf5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lglpk\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lgsl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lgslcblas\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{         }\PYGZhy{}DH5\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}110\PYGZus{}API\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}larmadillo
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each example exports its abstracted IMDP (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mdp.exportIMDP("\textless{}name\textgreater{}.imdp")}}) before
synthesis, which is the input used for the cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool comparison.


\subsection{Building and running the sparse driver}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/index:building-and-running-the-sparse-driver}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/sparse\_arch.cpp}} re\sphinxhyphen{}runs all cases through IMPaCT’s sparse abstraction
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/abstraction.cpp}}, O(nnz) memory) and the sparse OVI solver (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/solve.cpp}}). It
is pure standard C++ — no SYCL or Armadillo required:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
c++\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}std\PYG{o}{=}c++17\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O2\PYG{+w}{ }benchmarks/sparse\PYGZus{}arch.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }src/abstraction.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/solve.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/omaximization.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }src/graph\PYGZus{}utils.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}o\PYG{+w}{ }/tmp/sparse\PYGZus{}arch
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Run modes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
/tmp/sparse\PYGZus{}arch\PYG{+w}{              }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} FAST enclosure (corner\PYGZhy{}min + per\PYGZhy{}dimension max)}
/tmp/sparse\PYGZus{}arch\PYG{+w}{ }exact\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} EXACT/TIGHT enclosure (K=5\PYGZhy{}per\PYGZhy{}dim sub\PYGZhy{}grid)}
/tmp/sparse\PYGZus{}arch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{exactK}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{7}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} custom sub\PYGZhy{}grid density}
/tmp/sparse\PYGZus{}arch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{only}\PYG{o}{=}VP\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} run a single benchmark by name}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The driver aligns the sparse grid to the dense point\sphinxhyphen{}grid convention (cells centred on
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lb + k*eta}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(ub\sphinxhyphen{}lb)/eta + 1}} cells per dimension), so cell counts match the dense
abstraction exactly and values are directly comparable. For diagonal (uncoupled)
dynamics matrices the sparse mean enclosure is exact; for coupled dynamics it is a
sound over\sphinxhyphen{}approximation (see the BA page). For nonlinear dynamics the FAST/EXACT
modes control the tightness of the sampled mean enclosure (see the VP page).


\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/index:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only IMPaCT can abstract continuous dynamics into an IMDP; the peers solve IMPaCT’s
exported model. The pipeline is: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exportIMDP}} \(\rightarrow\) neutral \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} file \(\rightarrow\)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_to\_drn.py}} (Storm), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imdp\_to\_prism\_interval.py}} (PRISM),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intervalmdp\_runner.jl}} (IntervalMDP.jl), driven end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end by
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/crosstool/peers/sweep\_compare.py}}. All four tools agree on every ARCH
robust value; under the native finite horizons IMPaCT’s per\sphinxhyphen{}cell robust values match
IntervalMDP.jl to ≤ 2.3e\sphinxhyphen{}5 (≤ 7e\sphinxhyphen{}7 for the finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon cases).

\sphinxstepscope


\section{AS — Anaesthesia Delivery (3D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AS:as-anaesthesia-delivery-3d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AS::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The AS benchmark models automated anaesthesia delivery as a three\sphinxhyphen{}compartment
pharmacokinetic system with affine (linear) dynamics, two control inputs and additive
Gaussian noise. The specification is finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reachability: steer the drug
concentrations into a target box within 10 steps. Source:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/AS/AS.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AS:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (3D): compartment concentrations, gridded over
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1,6{]} x {[}0,10{]} x {[}0,10{]}}} with steps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0.25, 1, 1\}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input} (2D): infusion rates over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,7{]} x {[}0,30{]}}} with steps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{1, 30\}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: additive Gaussian, standard deviation \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(0.001)}} in each dimension.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification}: reach the target box \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}4,6{]} x {[}8,10{]} x {[}8,10{]}}} within horizon
H = 10 (robust/pessimistic).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Code walkthrough}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AS:code-walkthrough}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create the IMDP object and discretize the state and input spaces:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{mdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// label target cells, make absorbing}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Attach the dynamics and the noise model:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NORMAL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStdDev}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Build the abstraction — transition\sphinxhyphen{}probability intervals to the target region, to the
avoid region (here: leaving the grid), and between all cell pairs:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{targetTransitionVectorBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{transitionMatrixBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Export the abstracted IMDP for cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool comparison, then synthesize the
finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon controller (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} = pessimistic/robust) and save it:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{exportIMDP}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{AS.imdp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Build and run with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make \&\& ./AS}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/AS}}.


\subsection{Sparse\sphinxhyphen{}abstraction route}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AS:sparse-abstraction-route}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
AS is affine in the state, so the per\sphinxhyphen{}cell mean range is exact and the sparse
abstraction (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/sparse\_arch.cpp}}, run with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{only=AS}}) has no accuracy loss
per dimension. The driver aligns the sparse grid to the dense point\sphinxhyphen{}grid convention
so the cell counts match the dense abstraction exactly. Note that AS has a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{coupled} (non\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal) dynamics matrix: the sparse per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension product bound is
sound but slightly conservative compared with the dense joint NLopt optimisation
(see the BA page and ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0020 for the analysis).

Sparse path (single\sphinxhyphen{}threaded, pure C++): 0.83M nonzeros, \sphinxstylestrong{19.9 MB} versus a
1.02 GB dense matrix, building in 0.11 s and solving in \sphinxstylestrong{0.07 s} (versus 4.3 s
dense SYCL). After grid alignment the sparse interior mean is 0.0019 against the
dense (NLopt) 0.0045 — sound but conservative, as expected for coupled dynamics.


\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AS:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exported \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AS.imdp}} was solved by IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM and Storm on the identical
model. Under the native finite horizon (H = 10) IMPaCT’s per\sphinxhyphen{}cell robust values match
IntervalMDP.jl to \sphinxstylestrong{Δ ≤ 4.8e\sphinxhyphen{}7}. On the infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reachability reduction all
four tools return robust value 0 at the initial state (nothing is robustly reached in
the limit), with solve times 0.4 / 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.05 s
(IMPaCT / IntervalMDP.jl / PRISM / Storm).


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AS:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The dense finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon path recomputed a large \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{diff}} matrix each sweep; the
loop\sphinxhyphen{}invariant hoist was applied to the infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon functions, which is why
the sparse solve (0.07 s) is much faster than the dense SYCL solve (4.3 s) here.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PRISM rejects zero lower\sphinxhyphen{}bound interval edges, so its run used intervals floored to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1e\sphinxhyphen{}9, hi{]}}} — an ε\sphinxhyphen{}perturbation of the exported model.

\end{itemize}

\section{BA — Building Automation (4D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/BA:ba-building-automation-4d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/BA::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The BA benchmark is a four\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional building\sphinxhyphen{}automation (temperature\sphinxhyphen{}control)
system with affine dynamics, one heating input and additive Gaussian noise. The
specification is finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon safety: remain inside the temperature envelope for 6
steps. Source: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/BA/BA\_4d.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/BA:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (4D): two zone temperatures and two heater states, gridded over
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}19,21{]} x {[}19,21{]} x {[}30,36{]} x {[}30,36{]}}} with steps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0.5, 0.5, 1, 1\}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input} (1D): supply temperature over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}17,20{]}}} with step \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: additive Gaussian with per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension standard deviations
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(0.0774), sqrt(0.0774), sqrt(0.3872), sqrt(0.3098)}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification}: finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon safety, H = 6 — stay within the state grid
(leaving the grid is the avoid event).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dynamics are affine, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x\textquotesingle{} = A x + B u + Q}}:

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{xx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mat}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6682}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.02632}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\subsection{Code walkthrough}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/BA:code-walkthrough}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set up the spaces, dynamics and noise. A safety specification needs no target set —
only the probability intervals of \sphinxstyleemphasis{leaving} the safe grid:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{mdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NORMAL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStdDev}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Abstract the avoid vectors (probability of exiting the grid) and the cell\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}cell
transition matrices:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{transitionMatrixBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Export the IMDP and synthesize the robust finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon safety controller:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{exportIMDP}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{BA.imdp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{finiteHorizonSafeControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{6}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{// true = pessimistic}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Build and run with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make \&\& ./BA\_4d}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/BA}}.


\subsection{Sparse\sphinxhyphen{}abstraction route}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/BA:sparse-abstraction-route}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
BA is affine, so it runs through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/sparse\_arch.cpp}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{only=BA}}) with an
exact per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension mean range. With the grid aligned to the dense point\sphinxhyphen{}grid
convention the sparse cell count matches the dense abstraction exactly (1225 cells).

\sphinxAtStartPar
BA is the canonical \sphinxstyleemphasis{coupled\sphinxhyphen{}dynamics} case: because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} is non\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal, the sparse
box bound (product of per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension intervals) is a \sphinxstylestrong{sound over\sphinxhyphen{}approximation} —
the per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension worst cases are not jointly attainable — while the dense joint
NLopt optimisation is tighter. A one\sphinxhyphen{}step brute\sphinxhyphen{}force check on a corner cell gives a
true value of 0.2610 versus the sparse bound 0.2664 (+0.0054): both sound, sparse
slightly conservative. Grid alignment moved the sparse interior safety value from
0.107 to 0.348, against the dense (NLopt) 0.471.

\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/BA:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exported \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BA.imdp}} was solved identically by IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM and Storm.
Under the native finite horizon the initial\sphinxhyphen{}state robust safety value is \sphinxstylestrong{0.4533 in
all three tools} (IMPaCT, IntervalMDP.jl, Storm), and IMPaCT’s per\sphinxhyphen{}cell robust
values match IntervalMDP.jl to \sphinxstylestrong{Δ ≤ 4.3e\sphinxhyphen{}7}. On the infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon safety
reduction the robust value is 0, matching PRISM and Storm (verified at eps 1e\sphinxhyphen{}4);
IntervalMDP.jl reports 1.9e\sphinxhyphen{}4 at its defaults. Peer solve times: 4.9 / 0.3 / 0.7 s
(IntervalMDP.jl / PRISM / Storm).


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/BA:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{optimistic} infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon safety OVI did not converge within 180 s on
this model — a large safe end component (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0010, since resolved: topological Gauss\textendash{}Seidel brings the eps=1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 robust solve to 7.8 s). The robust (pessimistic)
value, which is the headline guarantee, is unambiguous and agrees across tools.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Optimistic safety is convention\sphinxhyphen{}dependent across tools (how the cooperative sense
resolves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}} leak edges); only the robust value should be compared directly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
BA’s noise window spans roughly 7 cells against a 4\sphinxhyphen{}cell domain, so low
finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon safety values are expected on this coarse grid.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{VP — Van der Pol Oscillator (2D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/VP:vp-van-der-pol-oscillator-2d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/VP::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The VP benchmark is an autonomous (input\sphinxhyphen{}free) two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional Van der Pol oscillator,
discretized in time with step 0.1, under additive Gaussian noise. The specification is
infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reachability of a small target box, making this a verification (rather
than control\sphinxhyphen{}synthesis) problem and the primary validation case for IMPaCT’s nonlinear
abstraction. Source: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/VP/VP.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/VP:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (2D): gridded over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}5,5{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}5,5{]}}} with step \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.2}} per dimension.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input}: none (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dim\_u = 0}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: additive Gaussian, standard deviation \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(0.04)}} per dimension.
(A custom uniform PDF is included in the source, commented out, as an example of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NoiseType::CUSTOM}}.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification}: infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reachability of
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1.2,\sphinxhyphen{}0.9{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}2.9,\sphinxhyphen{}2.0{]}}} (robust/pessimistic).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dynamics are the Euler\sphinxhyphen{}discretized Van der Pol equations — genuinely nonlinear:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{xx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Code walkthrough}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/VP:code-walkthrough}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No input space is set — this is verification of an autonomous system:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{mdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NORMAL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStdDev}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Abstraction — because the dynamics are nonlinear, the per\sphinxhyphen{}cell transition bounds are
computed by NLopt (a local optimiser, LN\_SBPLX by default; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{setAlgorithm}} can change
it):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{targetTransitionVectorBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{transitionMatrixBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{exportIMDP}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{VP.imdp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon synthesis. The default solver is sound interval iteration; the
example notes that \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ValueIteration}} (peer\sphinxhyphen{}style pure VI) uses far fewer sweeps:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{//mdp.setIterationMethod(IterationMethod::ValueIteration);   // optional}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infiniteHorizonReachControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{              }\PYG{c+c1}{// true = pessimistic}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

dense/IntervalMDP.jl reference 0.2297. The residual gap is the finite sub\sphinxhyphen{}grid
under\sphinxhyphen{}sampling the optimum the dense continuum optimiser finds — expected for
non\sphinxhyphen{}affine dynamics (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0021: for nonlinear \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{f}} both the sampled sparse enclosure
and the dense NLopt bound are heuristic; the validation is K\sphinxhyphen{}convergence plus
agreement with the dense/peer value).

\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/VP:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exported \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VP.imdp}} was solved by IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM and Storm on the identical
model. IMPaCT’s per\sphinxhyphen{}cell robust values match IntervalMDP.jl to \sphinxstylestrong{Δ ≤ 2.3e\sphinxhyphen{}5}. The
robust value at the initial state is 0 in all four tools, with solve times
1.8 / 0.55 / 1.4 / 0.04 s (IMPaCT / IntervalMDP.jl / PRISM / Storm).


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/VP:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
VP was the motivating case for adding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IterationMethod::ValueIteration}}: interval
iteration is a sound two\sphinxhyphen{}sided bracket but took 214 s before the loop\sphinxhyphen{}invariant
hoist (now 29.1 s); pure VI converges in 0.59 s with residual\sphinxhyphen{}based stopping.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0021 tracks a certified interval\sphinxhyphen{}arithmetic mean enclosure for nonlinear
dynamics, which would replace the sampled (heuristic) enclosure on the sparse path.

\end{itemize}

\section{IC — Integrator Chain (2D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/IC:ic-integrator-chain-2d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/IC::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The IC benchmark is a discrete\sphinxhyphen{}time double integrator (a two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional integrator
chain) with one bounded input and additive Gaussian noise. It comes in two variants
sharing the same dynamics: \sphinxstylestrong{IC\_reach} (finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reachability of a central box)
and \sphinxstylestrong{IC\_safe} (finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon safety). Sources:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/IC/IC\_reach\_2d.cpp}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IC\_safe\_2d.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/IC:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (2D): position and velocity, gridded over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}10,10{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}10,10{]}}} with step
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}} per dimension.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input} (1D): acceleration over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1,1{]}}} with step \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: additive Gaussian, standard deviation \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(0.01)}} per dimension.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specifications} (both robust/pessimistic, H = 5):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{IC\_reach}: reach the box \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}8,8{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}8,8{]}}} within 5 steps;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{IC\_safe}: remain within the state grid for 5 steps.

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dynamics are the sampled double integrator with sampling time \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Ns = 0.1}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{xx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kt}{float}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ns}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ns}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Ns}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{Ns}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{Ns}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{xx}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/IC:code-walkthrough}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both variants share the setup:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{mdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ss\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}lb}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}ub}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}eta}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setDynamics}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setNoise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{NoiseType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{NORMAL}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setStdDev}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sigma}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IC\_reach} labels the target region, abstracts target/avoid vectors and the
transition matrices, then synthesizes a robust finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reach controller:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{setTargetSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{target\PYGZus{}condition}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{targetTransitionVectorBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{transitionMatrixBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{exportIMDP}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{IC\PYGZus{}reach.imdp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{finiteHorizonReachControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{IC\_safe} needs no target set — only the avoid vectors (probability of leaving the
grid) and the transition matrices — and calls the safety synthesizer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{minAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{maxAvoidTransitionVector}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{transitionMatrixBounds}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{exportIMDP}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{IC\PYGZus{}safe.imdp}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{finiteHorizonSafeControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{mdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Build and run with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make \&\& ./IC\_reach\_2d}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./IC\_safe\_2d}}) in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/IC}}.

\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/IC:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exported IMDPs were solved by IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM and Storm on the identical
models. IMPaCT’s per\sphinxhyphen{}cell robust values match IntervalMDP.jl to \sphinxstylestrong{Δ ≤ 6.3e\sphinxhyphen{}7} for
both variants. On the infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reductions all four tools agree: robust reach
and safety are 0 at the initial state, and even the tiny optimistic reach value
agrees to high precision (IC\_reach opt ≈ 1.20e\sphinxhyphen{}26 in all four). Solve times
(IMPaCT / IntervalMDP.jl / PRISM / Storm): IC\_reach 0.1 / 0.4 / 0.2 / 0.05 s;
IC\_safe 0.15 / 0.5 / 0.06 / 0.02 s.


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/IC:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The v1 status of IC was “reduced (scale)”; the v2 runs above cover the 2D
configuration under both its native finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon specs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PRISM required flooring \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,hi{]}}} interval edges to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}1e\sphinxhyphen{}9,hi{]}}} (it rejects a zero
lower bound), so its values are an ε\sphinxhyphen{}perturbation of the exported model.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{PD — Package Delivery (2D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PD:pd-package-delivery-2d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PD::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The PD benchmark is a two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional package\sphinxhyphen{}delivery robot with stable diagonal
affine dynamics, two inputs and additive Gaussian noise. The ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP specification
is co\sphinxhyphen{}safe LTL; the shipped examples collapse it into two infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon
reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid problems with different targets — \sphinxstylestrong{PD\_p1} (deliver to the first drop\sphinxhyphen{}off)
and \sphinxstylestrong{PD\_p3} (deliver to the second) — around a common obstacle. Sources:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/PD/PD\_target\_p1.cpp}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PD\_target\_p3.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PD:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (2D): position, gridded over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}6,6{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}6,6{]}}} with step \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PD:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exported IMDPs were solved by IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM and Storm on the identical
models. The robust reach value is \sphinxstylestrong{1.0 in all four tools} for both PD\_p1 and PD\_p3;
for PD\_p1 the per\sphinxhyphen{}cell robust values match IntervalMDP.jl to \sphinxstylestrong{Δ ≤ 7.1e\sphinxhyphen{}7}. Solve
times (IMPaCT / IntervalMDP.jl / PRISM / Storm): PD\_p1 3.4 / 1.4 / 1.7 / 2.8 s;
PD\_p3 3.6 / 1.6 / 2.3 / 2.2 s.


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PD:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0003 (nature trap):} PD\_p3 exhibits a nature\sphinxhyphen{}confinable end component on
which interval iteration’s upper bound never contracts, so the default solver does
not converge. Two remedies ship in IMPaCT: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IterationMethod::ValueIteration}}
(converges, residual stopping) and \sphinxstylestrong{OptimisticVI} (OVI — default on the sparse
path, also available on the dense path via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{infiniteHorizonOVIDispatch}}), which is
both convergent and certified: dense\sphinxhyphen{}OVI on PD\_p3 returns the bracket
{[}0.9998, 1.0{]} with gap 1e\sphinxhyphen{}5 in 3.3 s. Empirically, MEC\sphinxhyphen{}collapse preprocessing does
\sphinxstyleemphasis{not} fix this — support\sphinxhyphen{}graph MECs miss nature\sphinxhyphen{}confinable end components; OVI or
robust\sphinxhyphen{}EC deflation is required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The on\sphinxhyphen{}disk examples are the co\sphinxhyphen{}safe LTL specification collapsed into separate
reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid targets (p1/p3); replacing this with a true DFA\sphinxhyphen{}product co\sphinxhyphen{}safe run is
the planned Phase\sphinxhyphen{}2 form of the benchmark.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{PR\_minimal — Patrol Robot (2D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PR_minimal:pr-minimal-patrol-robot-2d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PR_minimal::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The PR\_minimal benchmark is a reduced two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional patrol robot commanded by speed
and heading, with wide additive Gaussian noise, under an infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid
specification. It is the tool’s canonical \sphinxstyleemphasis{memory\sphinxhyphen{}wall} case: the dense abstraction
matrices reach 8.84 GB (an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}memory failure under a 4 GB cap, ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0006), and it
is the case that motivated the sparse abstraction path. Source:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/PR\_minimal/PR\_minimal.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PR_minimal:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (2D): position, gridded over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}10,10{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}10,10{]}}} with step \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.5}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input} (2D): speed and heading over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1,1{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1,1{]}}} with step \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.1}}
(441 actions).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: additive Gaussian, standard deviation \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(1/1.3333)}} (≈ 0.87) per
dimension — very wide relative to the 0.5 grid step.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification}: infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid — reach \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}5,8{]} x {[}5,8{]}}} while
avoiding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1.5,1.5{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1.5,1.5{]}}} (robust/pessimistic).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dynamics are affine in the state (identity) with a nonlinear input map:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

Note that the dense path needs a large\sphinxhyphen{}memory host (see Results).


\subsection{Sparse\sphinxhyphen{}abstraction route}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PR_minimal:sparse-abstraction-route}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Because the state part of the dynamics is the identity (diagonal), the sparse mean
enclosure in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/sparse\_arch.cpp}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{only=PR\_minimal}}) is \sphinxstylestrong{exact} — the
sparse abstraction matches the dense with no accuracy loss, at a fraction of the
memory. The nonlinearity lives entirely in the input map, which is evaluated per
discrete action. The driver skips PR\_minimal in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fast}} mode (its wide kernel makes it
the slowest case); run it explicitly with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{only=PR\_minimal}}.


\subsection{Results}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PR_minimal:results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dense SYCL path (AdaptiveCpp/OMP, 56 GB host): 1583 cells, abstraction \textasciitilde{}533 s using
two 8.84 GB dense matrices; the SYCL value iteration did not converge on this model.
Under a 4 GB memory cap the dense path is killed outright — the v1 baseline builds a
dense (state x input) x state matrix of 698103 x 1583 ≈ 8.84 GB (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0006).

\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PR_minimal:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PR\_minimal appears in the cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool study as an \sphinxstyleemphasis{abstraction\sphinxhyphen{}scalability} case: the
peer tools (IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM, Storm) cannot abstract continuous dynamics at all,
so building this IMDP is outside their scope, and it is not part of the four\sphinxhyphen{}tool
solve sweep. The exported \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} uses the same neutral format validated on the other
ARCH cases, where all four tools agree on every robust value.


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/PR_minimal:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0006:} the dense abstraction stores a (state x input) x state matrix for
each of the min/max bounds; PR\_minimal was the smallest shipped example that made
this infeasible on ordinary hardware, confirming the need for sparse storage.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The grid\sphinxhyphen{}aligned sparse abstraction is exact here (diagonal state dynamics), so the
sparse route is strictly preferable: identical model, 5x less memory, and it
completes the synthesis the dense SYCL solver could not.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{AV\_minimal — Autonomous Vehicle (3D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AV_minimal:av-minimal-autonomous-vehicle-3d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AV_minimal::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The AV\_minimal benchmark is a reduced three\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional autonomous vehicle — a
kinematic bicycle model with position and heading states, speed and steering inputs,
and wide additive Gaussian noise — under an infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid
specification. Like PR\_minimal it is primarily an abstraction\sphinxhyphen{}scalability case: the
dense matrices are 7.42 GB each, while the sparse path builds and solves the model.
Source: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/AV\_minimal/AV\_minimal.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AV_minimal:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (3D): planar position and heading, gridded over
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}5,5{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}5,5{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}3.4,3.4{]}}} with steps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0.5, 0.5, 0.4\}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input} (2D): speed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}1,4{]}}} (step 1) and steering angle \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}0.4,0.4{]}}} (step 0.2)
— 30 discrete actions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: additive Gaussian, standard deviation \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sqrt(1/1.5)}} (≈ 0.82) per
dimension — wide relative to the 0.5 grid step.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification}: infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid — reach the lane region
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}5.75,0.25{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}0.25,5.75{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}3.45,3.45{]}}} while avoiding the adjacent strip
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}5.75,0.25{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}0.75,\sphinxhyphen{}0.25{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}3.45,3.45{]}}} (robust/pessimistic).

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Sparse\sphinxhyphen{}abstraction route}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AV_minimal:sparse-abstraction-route}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
AV\_minimal is nonlinear in the state (through the heading), so the sparse path in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/sparse\_arch.cpp}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{only=AV\_minimal}}) uses the sampled mean enclosure:
FAST mode evaluates the dynamics at the source\sphinxhyphen{}cell corners; EXACT mode
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exact}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exactK=K}}) uses a K\sphinxhyphen{}per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension sub\sphinxhyphen{}grid for a tighter joint enclosure.
For non\sphinxhyphen{}affine dynamics this enclosure is heuristic (ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0021), validated by
K\sphinxhyphen{}convergence on the VP benchmark.

\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AV_minimal:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
AV\_minimal appears in the cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool study as an \sphinxstyleemphasis{abstraction\sphinxhyphen{}scalability} case:
building the IMDP from continuous dynamics is outside the scope of IntervalMDP.jl,
PRISM and Storm, and this model is not part of the four\sphinxhyphen{}tool solve sweep. The
exported \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} uses the same neutral format validated on the smaller ARCH cases,
where all four tools agree on every robust value.


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/AV_minimal:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The wide noise (σ ≈ 0.82 against η = 0.5) gives a kernel of roughly 10 cells per
dimension, hence \textasciitilde{}10\(\sp{\text{3}}\) successors per row; that makes the single\sphinxhyphen{}threaded OVI solve
heavy (1161 s), similar to PR\_minimal.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The modest robust reach value reflects the noise magnitude relative to the grid:
with noise this wide it is genuinely hard to \sphinxstyleemphasis{robustly} steer into the target, so
a low guaranteed lower bound is the sound answer, not an artefact.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0021 (certified interval\sphinxhyphen{}arithmetic mean enclosure) applies to this case: the
FAST corner sampling is a heuristic enclosure for non\sphinxhyphen{}affine dynamics.

\end{itemize}

\section{LM — Lane Merging Vehicle (6D)}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/LM:lm-lane-merging-vehicle-6d}}\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/LM::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The LM benchmark is a six\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional nonlinear lane\sphinxhyphen{}merging vehicle with two wheel
inputs, mostly deterministic dynamics (noise in only two of six dimensions), and a
long\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reachability specification (H = 200). It is the headline scalability
case of the suite: the dense abstraction is infeasible at roughly 96 GB per matrix,
while the sparse path builds and solves the model in about 40 s at 196 MB. Source:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/ARCH\sphinxhyphen{}COMP/2025/LM/LM.cpp}}.


\subsection{System}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/LM:system}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State} (6D): yaw rate, lateral velocity, planar position and two angle states,
gridded over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}0.5,0.5{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}0.5,0.5{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}10,4{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}5,4{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}3.14,3.14{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}3.14,3.14{]}}} with steps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 3.14, 3.14\}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input} (2D): wheel speeds over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0.5,3.5{]} x {[}0.5,3.5{]}}} with step \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.5}} per
dimension.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: Gaussian with standard deviation \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{0, 0, 0, 0, 0.001, 0.001\}}} — four of
the six dimensions are deterministic.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification}: finite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid with H = 200 — reach the merge point
(a box collapsed to the corner \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x2 = \sphinxhyphen{}10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x3 = \sphinxhyphen{}5}}) while avoiding the occupied
lane region \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}\sphinxhyphen{}0.5,0.5{]} x ... x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}4,4{]} x {[}2.5,4{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}3.14,3.14{]} x {[}\sphinxhyphen{}3.14,3.14{]}}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
In practice the dense build above cannot complete — use the sparse route below.


\subsection{Sparse\sphinxhyphen{}abstraction route}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/LM:sparse-abstraction-route}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LM is only feasible through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{benchmarks/sparse\_arch.cpp}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{only=LM}}). The dynamics
are nonlinear, so the sparse path samples the mean over each source cell: FAST mode
uses the 2\textasciicircum{}6 cell corners, EXACT mode (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exact}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exactK=K}}) a K\sphinxhyphen{}per\sphinxhyphen{}dimension
sub\sphinxhyphen{}grid (a heuristic enclosure for non\sphinxhyphen{}affine dynamics, ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0021). The driver
grid\sphinxhyphen{}aligns to the dense point\sphinxhyphen{}grid convention, applies the avoid region as dead
absorbing cells, and runs a 200\sphinxhyphen{}step robust value iteration.

\subsection{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool validation}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/LM:cross-tool-validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
LM appears in the cross\sphinxhyphen{}tool study as an \sphinxstyleemphasis{abstraction\sphinxhyphen{}scalability} case: no peer tool
(IntervalMDP.jl, PRISM, Storm) can abstract continuous dynamics, and the dense model
never existed to export, so LM is not part of the four\sphinxhyphen{}tool solve sweep. The sparse
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.imdp}} export uses the same neutral format validated on the smaller ARCH cases.


\subsection{Notes}
\label{\detokenize{benchmarks/LM:notes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The robust value 0.0000 is sound but vacuous.} Four of six dimensions have
σ = 0 (deterministic), so on this coarse grid the corner means of a cell scatter
into different destination cells, producing transition intervals \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0,1{]}}}; the
pessimistic (robust) lower bound of any such interval chain is 0. A finer grid
and/or the certified interval\sphinxhyphen{}arithmetic enclosure of ISSUE\sphinxhyphen{}0021 is needed to
obtain a non\sphinxhyphen{}trivial robust value on near\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic systems.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LM demonstrates why sparse storage is a prerequisite for higher\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional
benchmarks: nnz grows linearly in the number of cells (8.19M here), while the
dense min/max matrices grow quadratically (the driver’s dense estimate is
21.3 GB, and the dense IMDP class would need \textasciitilde{}96 GB per matrix on its grid).

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\end{itemize}

\section{GPU Synthesis}
\label{\detokenize{api/gpu-synthesis:gpu-synthesis}}\label{\detokenize{api/gpu-synthesis::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
GPU\sphinxhyphen{}accelerated synthesis functions are implemented in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{src/GPU\_synthesis.cpp}}
using SYCL via AdaptiveCpp. These are the \sphinxstylestrong{sorted} variants of the standard
synthesis algorithms.


\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{api/gpu-synthesis:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The sorted approach:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sorts states by transition probability, enabling efficient parallel reduction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Removes the dependency on the GLPK linear programming library

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enables execution on GPUs (NVIDIA, Intel, etc.) via SYCL

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All sorted synthesis functions are methods of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/imdp:_CPPv44IMDP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMDP}}}}} class.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{api/imdp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{IMDP (class IMDP)}}}} for the full function signatures.


\subsection{Usage}
\label{\detokenize{api/gpu-synthesis:usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To use GPU synthesis:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compute abstraction on CPU} and save to HDF5 files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Update the Makefile}: replace \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{IMDP.cpp}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GPU\_synthesis.cpp}}
and change \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}acpp\sphinxhyphen{}targets}} to your GPU target

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Load abstraction} from files and call sorted synthesis functions

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{IMDP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{imdp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}x}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}u}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dim\PYGZus{}w}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{c+c1}{// Load pre\PYGZhy{}computed data}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadStateSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ss.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadInputSpace}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{is.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMinTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{minTM.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{loadMaxTransitionMatrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{maxTM.h5}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{c+c1}{// ... load other vectors ...}

\PYG{c+c1}{// GPU\PYGZhy{}accelerated synthesis}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infiniteHorizonReachControllerSorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{imdp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{saveController}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Makefile Configuration}
\label{\detokenize{api/gpu-synthesis:makefile-configuration}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{CC}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }acpp
\PYG{n+nv}{CFLAGS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}acpp\PYGZhy{}targets\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}cuda:sm\PYGZus{}70\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}O3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}lnlopt\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}I/usr/include/hdf5/serial\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}L/usr/lib/x86\PYGZus{}64\PYGZhy{}linux\PYGZhy{}gnu/hdf5/serial\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}lhdf5\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lgsl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}lgslcblas\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}DH5\PYGZus{}USE\PYGZus{}110\PYGZus{}API\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}larmadillo

\PYG{n+nv}{SRCS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }example.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }../../src/GPU\PYGZus{}synthesis.cpp\PYG{+w}{ }../../src/MDP.cpp
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}lglpk}} is not needed for sorted synthesis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/gpu::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{GPU Setup}}}} for full GPU setup instructions.

\section{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{examples/index:examples}}\label{\detokenize{examples/index::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
IMPaCT includes a comprehensive set of examples demonstrating different
specifications, system dimensions, and features. Each example contains a
configuration file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.cpp}}), a Makefile, and MATLAB plotting scripts.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Smaller examples} (2D robot, 4D BAS) run on personal computers.
\sphinxstylestrong{Larger examples} (5D+) may require more powerful machines.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subsection{Reachability}
\label{\detokenize{examples/reachability:reachability}}\label{\detokenize{examples/reachability::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Synthesize a controller that drives the system to a target region.


\subsubsection{2D Robot — Undisturbed (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{ex\_2Drobot\sphinxhyphen{}R\sphinxhyphen{}U}})}
\label{\detokenize{examples/reachability:d-robot-undisturbed-ex-2drobot-r-u}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A 2D mobile robot navigates to a target region using synthesized control inputs.

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[width=400\sphinxpxdimen]{{fig2}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{System:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dimensions}: 2D state (position), 2D input (speed, angle)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{State space}: \([-10, 10]^2\), step size 1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Input space}: \([-1, 1]^2\), step size 0.2

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dynamics}: \(x_{k+1} = x_k + 2u_0 \cos(u_1),\; y_{k+1} = y_k + 2u_0 \sin(u_1)\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Noise}: Diagonal Gaussian, \(\sigma = \sqrt{1/1.333}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Target}: Square region \([5, 8]^2\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Specification}: Infinite\sphinxhyphen{}horizon reachability (pessimistic)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}2Drobot\PYGZhy{}R\PYGZhy{}U
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }./robot2D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the simplest example and serves as the basis for the {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting-started/quickstart::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Quick Start}}}}.


\subsubsection{2D Robot — Disturbed (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{ex\_2Drobot\sphinxhyphen{}R\sphinxhyphen{}D}})}
\label{\detokenize{examples/reachability:d-robot-disturbed-ex-2drobot-r-d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same system with an additive disturbance input. This is the most thoroughly
commented example and is recommended for understanding the configuration file format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Additional features:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2D disturbance space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Three\sphinxhyphen{}parameter dynamics: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{function\textless{}vec(const vec\&, const vec\&, const vec\&)\textgreater{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Demonstrates both infinite and finite horizon (finite is commented out)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}2Drobot\PYGZhy{}R\PYGZhy{}D
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }./robot2D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Reach\sphinxhyphen{}Avoid}
\label{\detokenize{examples/reach-avoid:reach-avoid}}\label{\detokenize{examples/reach-avoid::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Synthesize a controller that reaches a target region while avoiding unsafe regions.
IMPaCT automatically detects reach\sphinxhyphen{}avoid when both target and avoid regions are defined.


\subsubsection{2D Robot Reach\sphinxhyphen{}Avoid — Undisturbed (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{ex\_2Drobot\sphinxhyphen{}RA\sphinxhyphen{}U}})}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Target}: Green region

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Avoid}: Red region

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Safety}
\label{\detokenize{examples/safety:safety}}\label{\detokenize{examples/safety::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Synthesize a controller (or verify) that the system remains within a safe region.
In safety specifications, the entire state space is the safe region by default.


\subsubsection{3D Room Temperature (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{ex\_3Droom\sphinxhyphen{}S}})}
\label{\detokenize{examples/safety:d-room-temperature-ex-3droom-s}}
\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[width=500\sphinxpxdimen]{{fig3}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A 3D room temperature model is controlled to stay within safe temperature bounds
(shown by red dashes) over a finite time horizon of 10 steps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}3Droom\PYGZhy{}S
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }./room3D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{4D Building Automation (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{ex\_4DBAS\sphinxhyphen{}S}})}
\label{\detokenize{examples/safety:d-building-automation-ex-4dbas-s}}
\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[width=500\sphinxpxdimen]{{fig4}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A 4D building automation system controller maintains temperatures in 4 rooms
within safe bounds over 10 time steps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a small example suitable for personal computers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}4DBAS\PYGZhy{}S
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }./bas4D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{5D Room Temperature (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{ex\_5Droom\sphinxhyphen{}S}})}
\label{\detokenize{examples/safety:d-room-temperature-ex-5droom-s}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extension of the 3D room temperature model to 5 dimensions. Requires more
computational resources.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}5Droom\PYGZhy{}S
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }./room5D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{7D Building Automation — Verification (\sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{ex\_7DBAS\sphinxhyphen{}S}})}
\label{\detokenize{examples/safety:d-building-automation-verification-ex-7dbas-s}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A 7D building automation system with \sphinxstylestrong{no control inputs} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dim\_u = 0}}).
IMPaCT automatically performs \sphinxstylestrong{verification} (IMC) rather than synthesis,
returning satisfaction probabilities for each state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }examples/ex\PYGZus{}7DBAS\PYGZhy{}S
make\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }./bas7D
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
